model.name: Currency / Monetary Value
model.purpose: Provide an embeddable declaration of a monetary value on a host object: an exact decimal amount bound inseparably to an identified currency, with declared precision and rounding intent, an optional valuation date and conversion reference, and explicit value states, so that an agent can read, validate and reproduce monetary context without inferring any of it.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-032 is a mixin that a host object embeds when it needs to state a monetary value. Its boundary covers four concerns. (a) Currency identity: the code used, the authoritative catalogue and published edition it was resolved against, the code's class and status, and references to successor or redenominated codes. (b) Exact amount representation: sign, integer coefficient and decimal scale, canonical lexical form versus display form, zero and negative-zero handling, monetary intervals, and explicit exact, approximate, unknown, missing and not-applicable states. (c) Precision and valuation: the declared scale and rounding intent, the valuation date, and the reference to any conversion applied to reach the stated amount. (d) Governance of the mixin itself: ownership, catalogue pinning and integrity, supersession, and tombstoning of declarations. The model is never a currency master, a price, an account, a ledger entry, a payment, a transaction, a financial instrument or an economic event; it is the monetary field on someone else's object.
in_scope: Inseparable pairing of an exact amount with an identified currency reference on a host object
Currency code identity by alphabetic and numeric catalogue codes, with the catalogue and its published edition recorded
Code class and status as published by the catalogue: active, historic, registered fund, testing, precious metal and no-currency codes
References to successor or redenominated currency codes and to the catalogue amendment that recorded them
Exact decimal amount as sign, integer coefficient and scale, with canonical lexical form distinguished from display form
Declared scale, declared rounding intent and the digit bounds a host or profile imposes
Valuation date and the reference to any conversion applied, expressed as parameters of this declaration
Explicit value determinacy states and monetary interval endpoints, including explicit absence that is never expressed as zero
Governance of the mixin: catalogue pinning, integrity verification, supersession and tombstoning of the declaration
out_of_scope: Allocation, amendment, withdrawal or reinstatement of currency codes, which belong to the ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency
Publication, amendment and supersession of exchange-rate series by a treasury, central bank or market data publisher
Country, jurisdiction, legal-tender status, exchangeability, capital controls or purchasing power, none of which are derivable from a currency code
Locale formatting: symbols, decimal separators, grouping, cash rounding increments and localized currency names
Prices, quotes, fees, invoices, accounts, balances, ledger entries, journal postings, payments and settlement
Financial instruments, cash-flow schedules, valuation methodologies and accounting or tax treatment
Arithmetic execution, exception signalling and rounding-mode implementation by a numeric runtime
Enforcement of policy, runtime evaluation of rules and the storage or evaluation of audit trails
Digital-token or crypto-asset unit identity registers and community or complementary currency registers

boundary_notes.neighbor: ISO 4217 currency and funds code register (Maintenance Agency lists)
boundary_notes.distinction: The register owns allocation, amendment, withdrawal and the published minor-unit values; this mixin only carries a reference to a code plus the list and published edition it was resolved against, and re-states none of the register's lifecycle.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Locale display and formatting data (Unicode CLDR)
boundary_notes.distinction: Symbols, localized names, grouping, decimal separators and cash rounding increments are presentation owned by locale data; this mixin holds them only as optional labels and never treats a symbol as an identifier.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Financial message and payment models (ISO 20022 amount and currency types)
boundary_notes.distinction: Message profiles constrain amount digits and currency attributes for a payment instruction; this mixin defines the monetary declaration itself and owns no message, instruction or settlement lifecycle.

The publisher owns rate identity, effective periods, amendment and supersession; this mixin carries the valuation date and a reference to the rate used, and may derive a documented direct, inverse or cross-rate for a monetary calculation without becoming the publication authority for any source rate.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Host object that declares the money (price, fee, balance, budget line)
boundary_notes.distinction: The host owns record identity, record lifecycle and the business meaning of the amount, including what a negative amount signifies; this mixin owns only the shape and integrity of the monetary declaration it contributes.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Numeric arithmetic environment (IEEE 754 decimal formats, general decimal arithmetic)
boundary_notes.distinction: The arithmetic environment owns operations, rounding-mode execution and exception signalling; this mixin only fixes the abstract number model used to represent the declared amount exactly.

sources.title: Financial Data Standards - ISO 4217 (Currency codes)
sources.version_or_date: Accessed September 2026; states the January 2026 List One change for Bulgaria's euro adoption
sources.relevance: States that SIX is the official ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency and the only recognized authoritative source on currency code designations, and names the three published lists: List One (current currency and funds), List Two (fund codes registered with the agency) and List Three (historic currencies and funds).

sources.title: ISO 4217 List One: Current Currency & Funds (XML)
sources.relevance: Primary machine-readable code list. Root element ISO_4217 carries a Pblshd edition date; each entry carries CtryNm, CcyNm, Ccy (alphabetic), CcyNbr (numeric) and CcyMnrUnts. Evidence that minor units vary (USD 2, JPY 0, BHD 3, CLF 4) and are published as N.A. for precious metals (XAU, XAG, XPT, XPD), the testing code XTS, the no-currency code XXX and XDR.

sources.title: ISO 4217 List Three: Historic Currencies & Funds (XML)
sources.relevance: Primary evidence for withdrawn code identity and withdrawal timing. Historic entries carry CtryNm, CcyNm, Ccy, CcyNbr and WthdrwlDt, with withdrawal dates published at month granularity (for example DEM, FIM and GRD recorded as 2002-03) or as month ranges.

sources.title: XML Schema Part 2: Datatypes Second Edition - 3.2.3 decimal
sources.relevance: Defines the decimal value space as an integer multiplied by a non-positive power of ten, permits leading and trailing zeroes and an optional sign in the lexical space, defines a canonical representation that forbids a leading plus and requires a decimal point with at least one digit on each side, and defines the totalDigits and fractionDigits constraining facets.

sources.title: General Decimal Arithmetic Specification - The Arithmetic Model
sources.relevance: Publicly readable abstract model behind decimal floating-point arithmetic: a finite number is a sign (0 or 1), a zero-or-positive integer coefficient and a signed integer exponent, with value (-1)^sign x coefficient x 10^exponent. It permits numerically equal but visually distinct representations such as 1 and 1.00, and permits a negative zero (a zero coefficient with a non-zero sign).

sources.title: IEEE 754-2019 - IEEE Standard for Floating-Point Arithmetic
sources.organization: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
sources.relevance: Authoritative standard record. Its published scope covers interchange and arithmetic formats and methods for binary and decimal floating-point arithmetic, plus exception conditions and their default handling. Used only for the existence and scope of standardized decimal formats; clause text is behind a paywall and is not quoted.

sources.title: Unicode Technical Standard #35: Locale Data Markup Language, Part 3 Numbers - Currencies
sources.relevance: States that currency values should never be interchanged without a known currency code, warns that the same symbol may be used for multiple currencies and is therefore ambiguous, and defines supplemental currencyData attributes digits, rounding, cashDigits and cashRounding as formatting data. Also notes that CLDR's currency set deliberately diverges from ISO 4217 in both directions.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR Release 5 - Data Types: Money
sources.relevance: A widely implemented monetary datatype consisting of value (decimal, 0..1) and currency (code, 0..1) with a required binding to ISO 4217. It deliberately omits the comparator element present on Quantity, and requires implementations to preserve and respect the precision of a decimal as represented.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR Release 5 - ValueSet/CodeSystem DataAbsentReason
sources.version_or_date: FHIR v5.0.0 (R5), released 2023-03-26; code system URI http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/data-absent-reason
sources.relevance: A published vocabulary that separates distinct reasons a value is absent - unknown, asked-unknown, temp-unknown, not-asked, asked-declined, masked, not-applicable, unsupported, as-text, error, not-a-number, negative-infinity, positive-infinity, not-performed, not-permitted - demonstrating that absence is an explicit assertion rather than a numeric default.

sources.title: Generation of JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 for ISO 20022 (Technical Support Group document)
sources.organization: ISO 20022 Registration Authority / Technical Support Group
sources.relevance: Primary financial-messaging evidence that amount and currency form a single typed pair: ActiveCurrencyAndAmount and ActiveOrHistoricCurrencyAndAmount carry a currency attribute (Ccy) typed by ActiveCurrencyCode or ActiveOrHistoricCurrencyCode, and amounts are constrained by digit and minimum-value facets. It also shows that active and historic currency codes are separate typed vocabularies.

sources.title: schema.org MonetaryAmount
sources.relevance: Defines a monetary value or range with value, currency, minValue, maxValue, validFrom and validThrough, giving primary support for monetary interval endpoints on a host object. It also permits non-ISO currency identifiers such as cryptocurrency tickers and local exchange trading system names, which is a documented divergence from ISO 4217-only vocabularies.

sources.title: Treasury Reporting Rates of Exchange (dataset documentation)
sources.organization: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service
sources.version_or_date: Dataset last updated 2026-08-31; quarterly series covering 2001-03-31 onward
sources.relevance: A public-authority currency and rate list that identifies currencies by country and currency description rather than by ISO code, publishes a record date, and issues amended rates with new effective dates when rates deviate materially. Evidence that authoritative currency identity is catalogue-relative and that rate publication and supersession are owned by the publisher.

sources.title: Decimal Arithmetic Specification — Arithmetic operations (quantize, compare, divide-integer, remainder, round-to-integral-value)
sources.relevance: Defines quantize as setting the result exponent to that of a second operand and raising invalid-operation when the coefficient would exceed available precision; defines compare as treating numerically equal values with different exponents as equal; defines remainder and divide-integer for residual computation.

sources.title: Council Regulation (EC) No 1103/97 of 17 June 1997 on certain provisions relating to the introduction of the euro
sources.relevance: Statutory precision and rounding rules: conversion rates adopted with six significant figures, inverse rates prohibited, triangulation via an intermediate euro amount rounded to not less than three decimals, and final rounding to the nearest cent or sub-unit with exact half-way results rounded up.

sources.title: Rounding — consumer information on cash rounding in Ireland
sources.relevance: Official non-decimal cash quantization rule: totals round to the nearest 5 cent with stated endings (1–2 down, 3–4 up, 6–7 down, 8–9 up); rounding is voluntary, applies to the total bill and not individual prices, and does not apply to electronic payments.

sources.title: Eliminating the penny from Canada's coinage system (archived)
sources.organization: Government of Canada / Canada Revenue Agency
sources.version_or_date: archived page, last modified 22 June 2017 (penny withdrawn from circulation 4 February 2013)
sources.relevance: Second, independent official cash-rounding regime: cash transactions round to the nearest five-cent increment in a fair and transparent manner, only on the final bill of sale after tax, while cheques and card payments continue to settle to the cent; direction is stated as a principle rather than as fixed endings.

sources.title: Extensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) 2.1 Recommendation
sources.version_or_date: Recommendation of 31 December 2003, with errata corrected to 20 February 2013
sources.relevance: Normative separation of a reported number from its declared accuracy: mutually exclusive decimals and precision attributes (decimal places versus significant figures), an infinite-accuracy value for exactly stated numbers, and definitions covering rounding, truncation and decimal-place correctness.

sources.title: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0
sources.relevance: Implementation-level evidence of precision tiering and residual disclosure: document-level amounts are limited to two fraction digits and rounded to two decimals for accounting, unit prices carry no decimal restriction, parts of a line calculation are rounded separately, results derived from already-rounded amounts are not re-rounded, and a payable rounding amount element carries the residual explicitly.

sources.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/2104 amending Regulation (EC) No 1126/2008 as regards International Accounting Standards 1 and 8 (Definition of Material)
sources.version_or_date: OJ L 318, 10.12.2019, p. 74–78; subsequently consolidated into the later IFRS adoption regulation
sources.relevance: Endorsed definition of material — information is material if omitting, misstating or obscuring it could reasonably be expected to influence users' decisions — establishing that materiality depends on nature or magnitude and is a judgement made by the reporting entity, not a constant this model may supply.

sources.title: IAS 21 The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates
sources.organization: IFRS Foundation / International Accounting Standards Board
sources.version_or_date: Adopted April 2001, revised December 2003, amended August 2023 (Lack of Exchangeability); page state September 2026
sources.relevance: Normative source for functional currency, presentation currency, foreign currency, closing and spot rates, exchange differences and monetary items — the vocabulary behind amount roles and the requirement to translate at a rate tied to a specific date.

sources.title: IFRS 13 Fair Value Measurement
sources.organization: IFRS Foundation / International Accounting Standards Board
sources.relevance: Establishes that a value is defined by a measurement date, a market-participant assumption set and a principal or most advantageous market — the basis and market/scenario reference this model carries without implementing.

sources.title: Lack of Exchangeability (Amendments to IAS 21) — completed project
sources.organization: IFRS Foundation / International Accounting Standards Board
sources.relevance: Confirms an authoritative case where an estimated rather than observed spot rate must be asserted, requiring an explicit estimated status and disclosure rather than a silently substituted rate.

sources.title: Euro foreign exchange reference rates
sources.version_or_date: Daily publication regime; page accessed 3 September 2026
sources.relevance: Primary evidence for concertation time (around 14:10 CET), publication around 16:00 CET on working days except TARGET closing days, the EUR 1 = x quotation convention, the information-purposes-only statement discouraging transaction use, and suspension of a currency pair (EUR/RUB from 1 March 2022).

sources.title: ECB SDMX tutorial: using SDMX-ML to publish the euro foreign exchange reference rates
sources.version_or_date: ECB statistics co-operation and standards page; accessed 3 September 2026
sources.relevance: Documents the EXR key structure (FREQ, CURRENCY, CURRENCY_DENOM, EXR_TYPE, EXR_SUFFIX), the meaning of a key such as D.USD.EUR.SP00.A, observation-level TIME_PERIOD and OBS_VALUE, and attributes including OBS_STATUS, DECIMALS, UNIT and UNIT_MULT — the model for a resolvable rate reference and its stated precision.

sources.title: Extensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) 2.1 Recommendation
sources.relevance: Normative treatment of the unit element and measure for numeric items (section 4.8) and of accuracy attributes for reported numeric facts (sections 4.6.3-4.6.6), establishing that a monetary fact is meaningless without a declared unit and a declared accuracy.

sources.title: Precision, Decimals and Units 1.0 (Working Group Note)
sources.relevance: Explains that accuracy attributes describe the range in which the true value lies rather than a scaling instruction, that decimals='INF' expresses an exact monetary amount while decimals='2' implies rounding, that units must not embed implicit multipliers, and that rounding creates component-to-total inconsistency.

sources.title: RFC 3339 — Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Normative timestamp grammar requiring full-date, mandatory seconds and an explicit Z or numeric offset, and the interoperability argument that unqualified local time is unusable across the globe — the basis for separating valuation, effective, publication and ingestion instants.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/1011 on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts (Benchmarks Regulation)
sources.organization: European Parliament and Council of the European Union (via EUR-Lex)
sources.relevance: Defines benchmark, administrator, input data and methodology, and places governance, oversight, methodology transparency, methodology-change consultation, input-data monitoring and cessation procedures with the administrator — establishing that rate determination is a referenced, externally governed act.

sources.title: Foreign Exchange Rates — H.10 / G.5: About
sources.organization: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.version_or_date: H.10 weekly release, country data updated Mondays 4:15 p.m.; accessed 3 September 2026
sources.relevance: Independent authority publishing on an opposite convention (noon buying rates in New York for cable transfers, certified for customs purposes) and stating that past releases are not revised — direct evidence for explicit direction encoding and for divergent revision regimes.

sources.title: FX Global Code
sources.relevance: Global good-practice set for wholesale FX published by a partnership of central banks and market participants across 20 jurisdictions, aimed at a robust, fair, liquid, open and appropriately transparent market — supporting the requirement that pricing components remain separately identifiable rather than hidden inside a rate.

sources.title: OTC foreign exchange turnover in April 2025 — Triennial Central Bank Survey
sources.version_or_date: Preliminary results for April 2025 data; final data with the BIS Quarterly Review, December 2025
sources.relevance: Authoritative statement of currency-pair reporting convention (both sides of each transaction counted; USD on one side of 89.2% of trades) and of the instrument split between spot, forwards, swaps and options — evidence that a pair is two ordered currency roles and that instrument type is a neighbouring model's concern.

sources.title: IAS 21 The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates
sources.relevance: Defines functional currency, presentation currency, spot and closing rate, exchange difference and monetary items; grounds valuation instant, rate selection and the original-versus-translated value distinction, including estimation when a currency is not exchangeable.

sources.title: IFRS 13 Fair Value Measurement
sources.relevance: Establishes measurement date, observable versus unobservable input hierarchy and disclosure of valuation techniques; grounds valuation authority, measurement basis and input-quality declarations while keeping methodology outside this model.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Supplies entity/activity/agent, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, wasAssociatedWith, actedOnBehalfOf, wasRevisionOf and generatedAtTime as the alignment target for original-versus-derived value lineage and role attribution.

sources.title: eXtensible Access Control Markup Language (XACML) Version 3.0
sources.relevance: Separates policy decision from enforcement and defines subject/resource/action/environment attribute categories, obligations and advice; fixes the boundary that this model supplies attributes only and never renders or enforces decisions.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-162, Guide to Attribute Based Access Control (ABAC) Definition and Considerations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.relevance: Defines authorization as evaluation of subject, object, operation and environment attributes against policy; grounds publishing object attributes (sensitivity class, restriction basis, handling label) as the model's only access contribution.

sources.title: Universal Electronic Records Management (ERM) Requirements
sources.organization: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)
sources.relevance: Structures the electronic records lifecycle as capture, maintenance and use, disposal, transfer, metadata and reporting with Must Have / Should Have classification; grounds retention metadata and the separation of disposition readiness from disposal execution.

sources.title: 17 CFR 240.17a-4 - Records to be preserved by certain exchange members, brokers and dealers
sources.organization: U.S. Government Publishing Office / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
sources.version_or_date: Code of Federal Regulations, 2024 edition, Title 17, Volume 4
sources.relevance: Sets three- and six-year preservation periods, requires either non-rewriteable non-erasable preservation or an audit-trail alternative recording each modification, and requires records to stay readily accessible to examiners - the strongest constraint on correction-by-supersession.

sources.title: Taxable amount - VAT Directive 2006/112/EC (Article 91 currency conversion)
sources.organization: European Commission, Directorate-General for Taxation and Customs Union
sources.version_or_date: Consolidated VAT Directive 2006/112/EC, Article 91; page consulted 3 September 2026
sources.relevance: Shows a statutory rate-source mandate with Member State options (most representative market rate, latest ECB published rate subject to notification, or customs-value rules) - direct evidence that rate-source selection is jurisdictional and must be recorded per profile.

sources.title: AS 2201: An Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting That Is Integrated with An Audit of Financial Statements
sources.version_or_date: AS 2201, as amended by PCAOB Release No. 2024-005, effective 15 December 2026
sources.relevance: Requires controls over authorization, review and approval of significant transactions and period-end adjustments, notes limits on segregating duties in smaller entities and states that inquiry alone is insufficient evidence - grounds advisory role and segregation declarations and their evidence expectations.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
sources.relevance: Safe methods (9.2.1), idempotent methods (9.2.2), strong validators and ETag (8.8.3), If-Match (13.1.1) and If-Unmodified-Since (13.1.4), 412 Precondition Failed (15.5.13) and 409 Conflict (15.5.10). Grounds optimistic concurrency, precondition contracts and the read/write safety distinction independently of any transport choice.

sources.title: Federal Records Centers Program Freeze Process Overview / FAQ
sources.organization: National Archives and Records Administration (NARA), United States
sources.relevance: Defines a freeze as temporary suspension of scheduled disposition due to circumstances altering administrative, legal or fiscal value; the agency requests and lifts the freeze in writing and the records centre resumes disposition only after formal notification. Grounds hold semantics and the external ownership of destruction.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR Release 5 — RESTful API (http.html)
sources.version_or_date: FHIR R5 (5.0.0), normative RESTful API sections
sources.relevance: Version-aware update via ETag/If-Match with 409 or 412 on mismatch; conditional create via If-None-Exist; conditional update outcomes by match count; vread for prior versions; 410 Gone for deleted resources versus 404 for unknown; 422 for referential-integrity violations; controls on logical-id reuse. A worked, normative precedent for the operation contract.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR Release 5 — Data Types (Money, decimal precision)
sources.relevance: Money = value (decimal, implicit precision) + currency with a required binding to ISO 4217. States that decimal precision is significant (0.010 differs from 0.01) and that original precision must be preserved. Grounds verbatim amount/scale handling on read and the prohibition on silent re-scaling.

sources.title: Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0
sources.relevance: Issuer, credentialSubject, validFrom/validUntil, credentialStatus (status-list revocation) and securing proofs; credentials are not modified but revoked and reissued. Grounds review-evidence validity intervals, revocation checking and the correction-by-reissue pattern rather than in-place edit.

sources.title: The Idempotency-Key HTTP Header Field
sources.organization: Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) HTTP API Working Group
sources.relevance: Key uniqueness and non-reuse with a different payload, optional request fingerprinting, replay of the first recorded outcome, 409 for a duplicate arriving while the original is in flight, 422 for key reuse with a different payload, and a published expiry policy. Adopted here as a documented convention only — it is an expired draft, not a normative standard.

sources.title: RFC 9457: Problem Details for HTTP APIs
sources.relevance: Defines type, title, status, detail and instance members plus extension members for machine-readable error identification, with resolvable type URIs. Grounds the model's explicit, structured failure semantics independently of transport.

sources.title: Time Ontology in OWL
sources.relevance: TemporalEntity split into Instant and ProperInterval, hasBeginning/hasEnd, inXSDDateTimeStamp requiring a timezone, and the thirteen Allen interval relations including intervalMeets, intervalOverlaps and intervalDuring. Grounds interval containment, overlap and gap tests over an assertion's version series.

sources.title: Calculations 1.1
sources.relevance: Normative interval-based definition of calculation consistency derived from declared decimals, distinct round-to-nearest and truncation intervals, duplicate-fact handling and explicit inconsistency error codes — the basis for tolerance semantics in reconciliation.

sources.title: Council Regulation (EC) No 1103/97 on certain provisions relating to the introduction of the euro
sources.organization: Council of the European Union (via EUR-Lex)
sources.relevance: Binding arithmetic rules: conversion rates adopted with six significant figures, no rounding or truncation of the rate, prohibition on inverse rates and on direct bilateral rates, mandatory triangulation through the euro unit with an intermediate value rounded to not less than three decimals, and rounding of converted amounts to the nearest cent or sub-unit.

sources.title: Converting to the euro
sources.organization: European Commission, Directorate-General for Economic and Financial Affairs
sources.version_or_date: Current guidance page citing Council Regulation (EC) No 1103/97
sources.relevance: Authority restatement of the six-significant-figure rate rule, the prohibition on truncating or rounding the rate, the ban on direct bilateral conversion, the triangulation procedure and the nearest-cent rounding rule including the exactly-half-way case.

sources.title: Harmonised ISO 20022 data requirements for enhancing cross-border payments
sources.organization: Bank for International Settlements — Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures
sources.relevance: Establishes a consistent minimum data set for cross-border transactions in ISO 20022, evidencing that amount and currency semantics must survive end-to-end message projection and that fragmented local profiles are a recognised interoperability problem.

sources.title: Handbook on Statistical Disclosure Control — Glossary
sources.organization: SDC Center of Excellence (co-financed by Eurostat)
sources.relevance: Defines the recognised protection operations for aggregated (including monetary) tables — primary and secondary suppression, controlled and random rounding, interval publication, dominance rules and information loss — grounding the redacted/lossy export outcome.

bundles.name: Currency Reference Identity
bundles.description: How the currency component of a monetary declaration is identified: which authoritative catalogue and published edition governs the code, which code forms are used, what class and status the catalogue assigns, and how successor or redenominated codes are referenced without owning their lifecycle.
bundles.rationale: A monetary amount is meaningless without a currency, and a currency code is only interpretable relative to a named catalogue and a published edition of it. The maintenance agency publishes distinct lists for current, registered-fund and historic entries, publishes minor units that are sometimes not applicable, and publishes withdrawal dates at month granularity. Each of those facts changes how a consuming agent must resolve a code, so currency reference is a separate top-level concern from the numeric amount.

layers.name: Catalogue Binding and Code Form
layers.description: Which catalogue, list and published edition the currency code was resolved against, and which code forms (alphabetic, numeric) carry identity while symbols and localized names remain labels.

findings.name: Authoritative currency catalogue and pinned edition
findings.description: A currency code only identifies a currency relative to a named catalogue, a specific list within it and a published edition. The ISO 4217 lists carry an explicit published-edition attribute and are amended over time, so a declaration must record which catalogue, which list and which edition it was resolved against, and must be able to verify the retained snapshot before resolving anything against it.

questions.text: Which authoritative currency catalogue and maintaining authority governs the code used in this declaration?
answer_data: Maintenance authority named by the publisher

questions.text: Which published edition or snapshot of that catalogue was in force when this declaration was made?
answer_data: Publisher's edition or published date as published
Retrieval timestamp of the retained snapshot

questions.text: Which list within the catalogue supplied the entry: current currencies and funds, registered fund codes, or historic entries?
answer_data: List identifier and published list name
Entry position or key within the list
Whether the same code appears in more than one list

questions.text: How is the retained catalogue snapshot verified as unaltered before any code is resolved against it?
What must a consumer do when its own currency register differs from the catalogue named in this declaration?
answer_data: Declared catalogue identifier carried with the code
Mapping status between the two registers
Explicit unresolved marker when no mapping exists

data_elements.name: Currency catalogue identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the catalogue or register that governs the currency code, for example the ISO 4217 code register maintained by its Maintenance Agency.

data_elements.name: Catalogue published edition
data_elements.description: The publisher's own edition marker for the list used, such as the published date attribute carried on the ISO 4217 lists. Retained exactly as published, never re-derived.

data_elements.name: Catalogue list designator
data_elements.description: Which list within the catalogue supplied the entry: current currencies and funds, registered fund codes, or historic currencies and funds.

data_elements.name: Catalogue snapshot digest
data_elements.description: Content digest of the retained catalogue snapshot together with the algorithm name, used to prove the snapshot resolved against was unaltered.

artifacts.name: Retained currency catalogue snapshot
artifacts.description: A retained copy of the publisher's currency code list for one published edition, used so that a code resolved at declaration time can be reproduced later even after the publisher amends the list. The adopting Dimension retains it; the publisher continues to own its content and lifecycle.
media_or_form: Machine-readable code list as published by the maintenance agency
Tabular spreadsheet export of the same list
Publisher-independent normalized projection retained alongside the original
artifacts.identity_strategy: Publisher name plus published list designator plus the publisher's own published-edition marker; a content digest is recorded for integrity. The edition marker orders the series but is never used as the identifier of a declaration.

artifacts.name: Retained catalogue amendment notice
artifacts.description: A retained copy of a numbered amendment notice issued by the maintenance agency between full list editions, explaining why an entry's status, name or minor unit changed. Held as evidence for a status transition; the amendment's authority and lifecycle remain with the issuing agency.
media_or_form: Numbered amendment notice document as issued by the maintenance agency
Extracted change record referencing the affected codes
artifacts.identity_strategy: Issuing agency plus the agency's own amendment sequence number; ordering follows the agency sequence rather than retrieval order, and a content digest is recorded for integrity.

findings.name: Alphabetic and numeric code forms; symbols as labels only
findings.description: The catalogue publishes both an alphabetic code and a numeric code for an entry, and either may reach this declaration. Display symbols and localized currency names are ambiguous across currencies and must be carried, if at all, as presentation labels that never participate in identity or matching.

questions.text: Which alphabetic code and which numeric code identify the currency, and which form is authoritative for exchange here?
answer_data: Which form the declaration treats as primary

questions.text: What constraints govern an accepted code token: character set, length, case and permitted normalization?
answer_data: Rejection outcome for a non-conforming token

questions.text: Is any presented currency symbol or localized name recorded strictly as a display label rather than as an identifier?
answer_data: Locale tag the label belongs to
Explicit flag marking the string as non-identifying

questions.text: How are the alphabetic and numeric forms reconciled when the host supplies only one of them?
answer_data: Resolution rule applied against the pinned edition
Counterpart code returned by the lookup
Outcome recorded when the two forms disagree

data_elements.name: Alphabetic currency code
data_elements.description: The catalogue's alphabetic code for the currency, carried as the primary identifying token of the currency reference.

data_elements.name: Numeric currency code
data_elements.description: The catalogue's numeric code for the same entry, carried when a host system exchanges numeric rather than alphabetic tokens.

data_elements.name: Currency display label
data_elements.description: An optional symbol or localized currency name shown to a person. Explicitly non-identifying, because the same symbol may denote several currencies.

data_elements.name: Display label locale
data_elements.description: The locale a display label belongs to, recorded so that a label is never reused outside the locale that produced it.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Code forms and display labels are short inline field values on the host object plus a reference into the pinned catalogue snapshot declared elsewhere in this model. There is no separately identified, separately retained object here: producing one would duplicate the catalogue snapshot and create a second, competing source of code truth.

bundles.name: Exact Amount Representation and Declaration Integrity
bundles.description: How the numeric part of a monetary declaration is represented exactly, how its canonical form differs from any display form, how amount and currency stay inseparable on the host object, and how determinacy states and intervals are declared so that absence is never silently expressed as zero.
bundles.rationale: An exact decimal value space, a canonical lexical form and an explicit scale are all defined by published datatype and arithmetic specifications, and the same specifications show that numerically equal representations can differ visibly and that a signed zero exists. Separately, published monetary datatypes bind amount to currency as one type, published absent-value vocabularies show that absence is a distinct assertion, and published monetary vocabularies show that a monetary value may be an interval. These are representation and integrity concerns distinct from currency identity, so they form their own bundle.

layers.name: Exact Decimal Value and Canonical Form
layers.description: The abstract number model used for the amount, the digit bounds that constrain it, and the canonical lexical form that distinguishes a stored value from a rendered string.

findings.name: Exact decimal amount as sign, coefficient and scale
findings.description: The amount is an exact decimal value: a sign, a non-negative integer coefficient and a scale expressed as a non-positive power of ten. Binary floating point is rejected as the canonical representation because it cannot represent common decimal fractions exactly. Digit bounds on coefficient and scale are declared by the host or profile, and a value that cannot be represented exactly at the declared scale is rejected rather than rounded away.

bundles.name: Valuation assertion context
bundles.description: The context that turns an amount into an interpretable valuation: which role the amount plays, at which instant it is asserted to hold, on which declared measurement basis, and against which market or scenario.
bundles.rationale: IAS 21 makes an amount meaningful only relative to a currency role and a translation date, and IFRS 13 makes a value meaningful only relative to a measurement date, a market-participant assumption set and a market. Both place the defining act outside the amount itself, so the amount must carry an explicit, versioned frame rather than an implicit one.

layers.name: Amount role and temporal frame
layers.description: Declares which role a monetary amount occupies among the sibling amounts derived from one underlying value, and the instant at which that role-tagged amount is asserted to hold.

findings.name: Amount role pinned to a versioned classifier
findings.description: Every monetary amount declares its role — original/transaction, settlement, functional, presentation or reported — as a value drawn from a named classifier at a pinned version, so that role-tagged siblings derived from one underlying value coexist and a converted amount can never silently stand in for the original.

It has no document form, no rendition and no lifecycle of its own; materialising it as an artifact would create a second identity for something that is already an attribute of the amount held by the owning record.

layers.name: Measurement basis and market or scenario reference
layers.description: Captures which measurement basis was asserted, who is entitled to designate it, which market, venue, session or scenario it refers to, and how a non-exchangeable currency is handled — all as references, never as an implementation of the basis.

findings.description: Records the asserted measurement basis (for example historical cost at the transaction-date rate, closing rate, period average, or fair value at a measurement date), the standard or policy that defines it, the authority entitled to designate it, and the market, venue, session or scenario the valuation refers to, including the case where the currency is not exchangeable and an estimated rate must be asserted.

Creating a local artifact for a basis would import the defining standard's content into this model and invite drift from the authoritative text; a versioned reference plus the designation decision is the complete and falsifiable representation.

bundles.name: Exchange rate quotation context
bundles.description: Everything needed to interpret an exchange rate applied to a valuation: which currencies in which direction under which unit convention, at what value and precision, from which source under which methodology, for which market session, valid over which interval, and at what quality status.
bundles.rationale: Authoritative publishers disagree on direction and revision policy — the ECB quotes EUR 1 = x foreign currency units and discourages transaction use, while the Federal Reserve publishes New York noon buying rates and does not revise past releases. A rate value stored without explicit base, quote, direction, source, session, validity and status is therefore not interpretable and not reproducible.

layers.name: Currency pair, direction and quoted value
layers.description: Fixes which currency is base and which is quote, how many base units the rate prices, whether the stored value is the published direction or an inversion, and the numeric value with its declared accuracy.

findings.name: Base and quote currency, unit convention and rate value precision
findings.description: Records the ordered currency pair with an explicit unit convention (how many units of quote currency price N units of base currency), whether the stored value is as published or inverted, and the rate value together with the number of decimal places to which it is accurate — never a bare number whose direction is inferred from field naming.

questions.text: Which currency is base and which is quote for this quotation, and how many base units does the rate value price?
answer_data: Number of base currency units priced by the rate value

questions.text: What is the rate value and to how many decimal places is it accurate as published?
answer_data: Rate value as an exact decimal
Declared decimals or accuracy statement from the publisher
Whether the published value is exact or rounded

questions.text: Is the stored rate held in the publisher's direction or as an inverted value, and how is inversion flagged?
answer_data: Inversion indicator and the inversion precision rule
Prohibition on storing an inverted value in place of the published one

questions.text: How does the stored direction map to a consumer or publisher whose quotation convention is the opposite?
answer_data: Mapping rule to the consumer's convention
Round-trip tolerance when inversion and re-inversion are applied

data_elements.name: Base currency code
data_elements.description: ISO 4217 code of the currency whose units are priced by the rate.

data_elements.name: Quote currency code
data_elements.description: ISO 4217 code of the currency in which the price of the base currency is expressed.

data_elements.name: Rate unit count
data_elements.description: Number of base currency units the rate value prices, typically one but explicitly recorded for currencies quoted per hundred or per thousand.

data_elements.name: Rate value
data_elements.description: Exact decimal rate value as published in the publisher's direction, stored without any scaling multiplier.

data_elements.name: Rate declared accuracy
data_elements.description: Number of decimal places to which the rate value is accurate, or an exactness marker where the publisher states the value is exact.

data_elements.name: Rate inversion indicator
data_elements.description: Marks a stored value derived by inverting the published direction, retained alongside rather than replacing the published value.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Direction, unit convention and value are the smallest queryable fields on which every downstream calculation depends; they must be filterable and comparable rather than embedded in a document. The publisher's own rendition is captured separately under reproducibility evidence, so no artifact is needed here.

bundles.name: Conversion derivation, linkage and assurance
bundles.description: How a converted amount is derived from an original, what equation and rounding order produced it, how original, converted and separately referenced charges relate, what evidence makes the result reproducible, and how a valuation assertion is corrected or superseded.
bundles.rationale: XBRL guidance shows that rounding order and declared accuracy determine whether reported components reconcile at all, ECB practice makes cross rates a derived rather than published quantity, and the divergent revision regimes of the Federal Reserve and EU benchmark administrators mean a valuation must carry its own correction semantics rather than inheriting the publisher's.

layers.name: Derivation, computation and amount linkage
layers.description: The mechanics of arriving at a converted amount and of relating it to the preserved original and to separately referenced charge components.

findings.name: Derivation method and ordered rate chain
findings.description: Declares whether the applied rate is direct, inverse, cross or triangulated, and where it is not direct, the ordered chain of constituent rate references with pivot currencies, so that a cross rate is recognisable as a derived quantity rather than a published one.

questions.text: Is the applied rate direct, inverse, cross or triangulated?
answer_data: Justification for not using a direct quotation where one exists

questions.text: Which ordered constituent rates and pivot currencies make up the chain used to reach the target currency?

questions.text: At which steps of the chain is intermediate rounding permitted, and at which is it prohibited?
answer_data: Rule owner for the chain rounding policy

questions.text: How is the derived chain result checked against an independently published direct quotation when one exists?
answer_data: Reference to the independent direct quotation
Permitted divergence between chained and direct results
Action taken when divergence exceeds the threshold

data_elements.name: Rate chain step
