bundles.name: Authority, accountability and monetary assertion lifecycle
bundles.description: Who may assert, correct or re-base a monetary value on its host, how that assertion is identified without an independent identity, and how it is versioned, made effective, corrected and superseded against pinned normative references.
bundles.rationale: Authorization of transactions and review/approval of period-end adjustments are control objectives in their own right (SRC-040), while the identity of a monetary fact is derived from concept, context and unit rather than from a standalone key (SRC-017). Currency code lists change by published amendment (SRC-001) and mandated rate sources differ by jurisdiction (SRC-039), so version pinning belongs with lifecycle rather than with representation.

layers.name: Accountable roles and change authority
layers.description: Advisory declarations of who is accountable for a monetary value and who is competent to change its amount, its currency, its rate source or the rounding policy applied to it.

findings.name: Accountable roles and segregation of duties
findings.description: Declaration of the parties associated with a monetary assertion - accountable value owner, currency-data steward, valuation authority, preparer, independent reviewer and approver - and of whether those positions are held by distinct parties. All declarations are advisory metadata; no permission is granted or withheld here.

questions.text: Which party is recorded as accountable for this monetary value on its host record, and over what interval?
Which function stewards the currency code list and rounding configuration, and which body is named as the valuation authority for the basis applied?
Are preparer, independent reviewer and approver held by distinct parties for this assertion?
Under which declared rule may one party hold more than one of these positions, and what compensating declaration is then recorded?
What evidence supports each declared role assignment where the reviewer relied on an automated check rather than re-performance?

data_elements.name: Accountable party reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the party recorded as accountable for the monetary value on its host; optional, because no source requires a single owner for every monetary value.

data_elements.name: Role assignment entry
data_elements.description: An advisory association of a party with one role (steward, valuation authority, preparer, reviewer, approver) over an effective interval, shaped for PROV attribution and delegation.

data_elements.name: Segregation relief declaration
data_elements.description: Recorded rule reference, combined positions and compensating measure where duties cannot be segregated, as anticipated for smaller or less complex entities.

data_elements.name: Review and approval state
data_elements.description: Observable state code for the review and approval position of the assertion, so that approval is never inferred from the mere presence of a value.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Role and segregation declarations are structured reference data pointing at party records held elsewhere; they carry no rendered content of their own and produce no document. Materialising them as artifacts would duplicate the party register and imply that this model holds the authoritative personnel record, which it does not.

findings.name: Authority for amount correction, currency and rate-source selection, and rounding policy
findings.description: Declaration of the authority under which an existing amount or currency may be corrected, under which a rate source is chosen, and under which the rounding and minor-unit policy applied to the value may be changed - including whether that authority is jurisdictional or entity-internal.

questions.text: Which authority record permits a correction to the amount or currency of an existing monetary assertion?
On what basis was the exchange-rate source selected, and is the selection mandated by a jurisdictional rule or chosen under entity policy?
Which rounding and minor-unit policy version applies, and who is competent to change it?
What is recorded when the mandated rate source publishes nothing for the required instant or the currency is not exchangeable at the measurement date?

data_elements.name: Change authority reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the authority record (delegation, policy or statutory rule) relied on for a correction or re-basing of the value.

data_elements.name: Rate-source selection basis
data_elements.description: Code distinguishing a statutorily mandated source, a framework-required spot or closing rate, and an entity-policy choice.

data_elements.name: Rounding policy reference
data_elements.description: Reference plus version of the rounding and minor-unit policy applied; the ISO 4217 minor unit is an input to that policy, not the policy itself.

data_elements.name: Rate fallback declaration
data_elements.description: Record of the substitute source, estimation basis or deviation applied when the mandated source or an exchange rate was unavailable.

artifacts.name: Monetary change-authority declaration
artifacts.description: A dated statement naming the authority relied on for amount correction, rate-source selection and rounding-policy change, with its scope and expiry. It records authority; it does not evaluate or enforce it.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative identifier of the issuing governance system's policy or delegation record; otherwise a Dimension-assigned ULID.

layers.name: Assertion identity, versioning and normative pins
layers.description: How a monetary assertion is identified through its host, how its versions and effective intervals are managed, and which external code-list and policy versions were in force when it was made.

findings.name: Host-dependent weak identity of a monetary assertion
findings.description: A monetary value has no independent existence: it is identified by its host record, the role it plays on that host, its currency and its valuation context, mirroring how a reported monetary fact is identified by concept, context and unit. A valuation date is context, never an identifier.

questions.text: Which combination of host reference, role on the host, currency and valuation context uniquely identifies this monetary assertion?
Under which conditions must the adopting Dimension mint a surrogate identifier instead of relying on the host key?
How is this assertion distinguished from another that merely carries the same amount and the same currency?
Is the monetary assertion an inseparable component of the host record or a separately addressable record?

data_elements.name: Host record reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the record the monetary value is attached to; mandatory because the mixin has no standalone existence.

data_elements.name: Role on host
data_elements.description: Code for the position the value occupies on its host (for example gross amount, tax amount, translated amount), which discriminates same-valued siblings.

data_elements.name: Identity component set
data_elements.description: Ordered list naming the attributes that jointly identify the assertion (host reference, role, currency, valuation context), used for collision checks.

data_elements.name: Dimension-assigned surrogate identifier
data_elements.description: UUID or ULID minted only when the host key is unavailable or unstable; never derived from a date.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity here is a key definition and a set of pointer fields evaluated at read time. Emitting an artifact would create a second, competing identity anchor for something that is deliberately dependent on its host, and would invite systems to treat the monetary value as an independent master record.

findings.name: Version, effective interval, correction and supersession
findings.description: Lifecycle verbs govern the monetary binding on its host - asserted, revised, superseded, withdrawn - and never the currency, the rate feed, the transaction, the account or the instrument. Where preservation rules forbid rewriting, correction is expressed as an additive superseding version.

questions.text: Which lifecycle states may a monetary assertion occupy on its host, and which transitions between them are permitted?
How are the interval over which the asserted value is effective and the instant at which it was recorded represented separately?
When a corrected amount is issued, is the prior assertion overwritten or retained as an immutable superseded version?
Which external record must be cited when the change is driven by an event this model does not own, such as a restatement or a re-issued source document?

data_elements.name: Assertion status
data_elements.description: State of the monetary binding on its host (for example asserted, superseded, withdrawn); scoped to the binding, not to any external object.

data_elements.name: Effective interval
data_elements.description: Start and optional end of the interval over which the asserted value holds, expressed with explicit offsets.

data_elements.name: Recorded-at timestamp
data_elements.description: Instant at which the assertion was recorded in the holding system, kept distinct from the valuation instant and from the rate observation time.

data_elements.name: Superseded assertion reference
data_elements.description: Reference from a corrected assertion to the version it replaces, aligned with a provenance revision relation.

data_elements.name: External change trigger reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the externally owned record that occasioned the change; this model records the pointer, not the external record's own lifecycle.

artifacts.name: Monetary assertion revision note
artifacts.description: A per-revision note recording what changed, the authority cited, the trigger and the superseded version, retained additively so that no prior value is erased.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Host key plus role plus zero-padded monotonic revision sequence; the sequence number never encodes a date.

findings.name: Currency-list and policy version pins
findings.description: Record of which ISO 4217 code-list edition and amendment, and which rounding, rate-source and accounting-profile policy versions, were in force when the assertion was made - so the value stays interpretable after those references change. The register's own lifecycle stays with its maintenance agency.

questions.text: Which ISO 4217 code-list edition and amendment number were in force when this currency code was resolved?
How does a value citing a withdrawn or replaced currency code remain interpretable after the register publishes the replacement?
Which policy versions - rounding, rate-source rule and accounting profile - are pinned to this assertion?
How is a pin recorded when the referenced register or policy publishes no version identifier?

data_elements.name: Currency code-list pin
data_elements.description: Edition, amendment number and list identifier of the ISO 4217 code list used to resolve the currency, with the resolution time.

data_elements.name: Currency code status
data_elements.description: Whether the cited code is current, a fund code or a historic code under the maintenance agency's published lists.

data_elements.name: Policy version pin
data_elements.description: Reference and version label of each governing policy in force at assertion time, plus a content digest when the source is unversioned.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Pins are short structured references whose authoritative content lives in externally published lists and policy registers. Copying those lists into local artifacts would fork a normative register that the maintenance agency alone may amend, and would create stale duplicates of material this model must only cite.

bundles.name: Provenance, protection, retention and interoperability of monetary context
bundles.description: How an original or derived monetary value is attributed and evidenced, how its confidentiality and access scopes are declared, how long the context is kept and what survives disposition, and how it is mapped to external representations under regional and accounting profiles.
bundles.rationale: Derivation, attribution and delegation relations are standardised (SRC-034); rate publishers attach explicit usage limitations that must travel with the value (SRC-023); preservation format and accessibility duties apply to financial records (SRC-038) within a lifecycle whose disposal step belongs to the records programme (SRC-037); and access decisions are made by an external decision point from published attributes (SRC-035, SRC-036).

layers.name: Value provenance and evidence integrity
layers.description: Lineage from original to derived monetary values, attribution of responsibility, and the integrity and limitations of the evidence that supports them.

findings.name: Provenance of original and derived monetary values
findings.description: Lineage of a monetary value: which original amount it came from, which conversion, translation, re-measurement or allocation produced it, which rate was applied and for which instant, and which agent is responsible - shaped to entity/activity/agent provenance relations.

questions.text: From which original value, by which activity and with which applied rate was this derived monetary value produced?
Which agent is attributed responsibility for the derived value, and on whose behalf did that agent act?
Which instant does the applied rate refer to, and when was it retrieved from its publisher?
Is the recorded value an as-transacted amount, a translated amount or a re-measured amount?
What tolerance is accepted between a value recomputed from the lineage and the stored value?

data_elements.name: Original value reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the as-stated monetary value from which this value was derived; absent when the value is itself original.

data_elements.name: Derivation activity
data_elements.description: Type, parameters and time of the activity that produced the derived value (conversion, translation, re-measurement, allocation).

data_elements.name: Applied rate source reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the publisher and series of the rate applied, together with any publisher-stated usage limitation.

data_elements.name: Rate reference instant
data_elements.description: The instant the applied rate refers to, distinct from the instant the rate was retrieved and from the recorded-at time.

data_elements.name: Measurement basis
data_elements.description: Code stating whether the amount is as transacted, translated at a spot or closing rate, or re-measured on another basis.

data_elements.name: Attributed agent reference
data_elements.description: Agent responsible for producing the value, with optional delegation to the agent it acted on behalf of.

artifacts.name: Conversion lineage record
artifacts.description: A record binding the original value, derivation activity, applied rate, rate instant and attributed agent so that a derived value can be independently recomputed and challenged.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Derived assertion key plus derivation activity identifier; falls back to a Dimension-assigned ULID where the activity is unidentified.

findings.name: Evidence integrity, audit references and stated limitations
findings.description: Integrity declarations for the evidence supporting a monetary value (rate snapshots, source documents, approval records), references to external audit or assurance records, and explicit limitations - including that a rate published for information only cannot be presented as a transaction rate. This model holds neither the audit trail nor the audit conclusion.

questions.text: Which integrity check value and algorithm are recorded for each evidence item supporting this value?
How is the completeness of the evidence set for a monetary assertion checked declaratively?
Which limitation must be stated when the supporting rate is published for information purposes only?
What is recorded when evidence is missing, superseded, or supplied by a party with an interest in the value?
Which external audit or assurance record is cited, and what does this model deliberately not assert about it?

data_elements.name: Evidence item entry
data_elements.description: Reference, kind and origin of one item of supporting evidence for the monetary assertion.

data_elements.name: Evidence integrity digest
data_elements.description: Digest value and algorithm recorded for an evidence item, supporting later detection of modification without asserting that any control operated.

data_elements.name: External audit record reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to an audit or assurance record concerning the value or its controls; the reference conveys existence and scope only.

data_elements.name: Evidence limitation note
data_elements.description: Statement of the declared limits of an evidence item, such as a publisher's information-only qualification on a reference rate.

artifacts.name: Rate evidence snapshot
artifacts.description: A captured copy of the rate quotation relied on, with publisher, series, reference instant, retrieval time and any usage limitation as published.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Rate source identifier plus series plus rate reference instant, with a zero-padded capture sequence for repeated captures of the same instant.

artifacts.name: Evidence integrity manifest
artifacts.description: A manifest listing each evidence item with its digest, algorithm and computation time, enabling recomputation and comparison without altering the evidence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Assertion key plus manifest revision reference; no date component is used as the identifier.

layers.name: Sensitivity classification and access scoping
layers.description: Confidentiality classification of monetary values and the attributes and scopes this model publishes so that an external decision point can evaluate a request.

findings.name: Sensitive or commercially restricted values and access scopes
findings.description: Classification of monetary values that are commercially restricted or otherwise sensitive, the handling labels that must travel with them, and the declaration of access constraints at bundle, layer, finding and artifact scope. The model contributes attributes only; decision and enforcement remain with the external authorization component.

questions.text: Which sensitivity class applies, and does it attach to the amount, the currency, the counterparty or the derivation?
Which values are commercially restricted such that disclosure would breach a contractual confidentiality term?
Which resource and environment attributes must this model expose so that an external decision point can evaluate a request?
How is a required masked, banded or rounded projection of a restricted amount declared without asserting that masking has been applied?
Which time-bounded exceptions permit broader access, for example to a regulator or an external auditor?

data_elements.name: Sensitivity class
data_elements.description: Classification code for the monetary value, used as an object attribute by an external decision point.

data_elements.name: Commercial restriction basis
data_elements.description: Code and agreement reference explaining why the value is commercially restricted.

data_elements.name: Declared access scope
data_elements.description: The scope at which an access constraint is declared: bundle, layer, finding or artifact.

data_elements.name: Handling label
data_elements.description: Label that must accompany the value when projected into another system, carried as advisory metadata.

data_elements.name: Access exception declaration
data_elements.description: Time-bounded declaration of a broader-access basis, such as regulatory examination access to preserved records.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are attribute declarations consumed at request time by an external policy decision point; they have no standalone rendered form. Producing an artifact would encourage the model to be treated as a policy store or as the record of an access decision, which would take ownership of evaluation and enforcement that belong to the authorization component.

layers.name: Retention, disposition and profile interoperability
layers.description: How long monetary context and its evidence are kept, what survives disposition, and how the value is declared against regional and accounting profiles and mapped to external representations.

findings.name: Retention class, legal hold and tombstone
findings.description: Declaration of the retention class and trigger for this model's own monetary context records and evidence, the presence and source of a legal hold that suppresses disposition, and the tombstone content retained after disposal. Disposal execution, transfer and destruction evidence belong to the records programme.

questions.text: Which retention class, trigger event and minimum period apply to this monetary context record and its evidence?
How is a legal hold recorded so that disposition is suppressed, and which external authority issued it?
Which end-of-life states may the record occupy, and which fields survive in a tombstone after disposal?
Which system executes disposal, and what does this model record as evidence that disposition occurred?
How are retention obligations reconciled when the host record and the monetary assertion carry different periods?

data_elements.name: Retention class
data_elements.description: Classification assigning the monetary context record to a retention schedule owned by the records programme.

data_elements.name: Retention trigger event
data_elements.description: The event that starts the retention clock, such as record creation or closure of the host transaction.

data_elements.name: Legal hold flag
data_elements.description: Boolean declaring that disposition is suppressed; the decision to impose or release the hold is made outside this model.

data_elements.name: Hold authority reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the instruction or authority under which the hold was imposed.

data_elements.name: Tombstone content
data_elements.description: The minimal surviving record after disposal: assertion key, host reference, currency code, retention class, disposition time and disposition record reference, with amount and evidence removed.

data_elements.name: Disposition record reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the externally held record evidencing that disposal was carried out.

artifacts.name: Monetary context tombstone record
artifacts.description: The surviving stub for a disposed monetary context record, preserving identity and disposition facts while carrying no amount or evidence content.
artifacts.identity_strategy: The assertion key of the disposed record, preserved unchanged so that inbound references resolve to a tombstone rather than dangling.

findings.name: Regional and accounting profile declaration and interoperability mappings
findings.description: Declaration of the regional, tax or accounting profile that governs a value - including functional and presentation currency roles and statutory conversion rules - and of the mappings to external representations, each labelled as an alignment or an evidenced conformance claim, with declared losses.

questions.text: Which regional, tax or accounting profile governs this value, and which currency roles does it assign?
To which external representations is this monetary context mapped, and is each mapping an alignment or a claim of conformance?
Where the external representation cannot express a local field, what loss is declared and what round-trip behaviour is expected?
Which rule takes precedence when two profiles mandate different rate sources for the same underlying value?
Which checks must pass before a conformance claim, rather than an alignment, may be recorded?

data_elements.name: Governing profile reference
data_elements.description: Reference and version of the regional, tax or accounting profile governing the value's currency roles and conversion rule.

data_elements.name: Interoperability mapping entry
data_elements.description: Pairing of a local field with a field in an external representation, labelled as alignment or conformance.

data_elements.name: Declared mapping loss
data_elements.description: Statement of information that cannot survive a mapping, such as pins or limitation notes with no target field.

data_elements.name: Profile precedence rule reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the rule resolving competing profile mandates, or an indicator that two mandated values must coexist.

artifacts.name: Profile conformance statement
artifacts.description: A statement naming the profile, its version, the checks performed and whether the result is an alignment or an evidenced conformance claim.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Profile reference plus profile version plus the identifier of the model release the statement was made against.

artifacts.name: External representation mapping table
artifacts.description: A field-level mapping table between this model's monetary context and an external representation, including unmapped fields and declared losses.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Target representation identifier plus target version; a Dimension-assigned ULID is used when the target publishes no version.

bundles.name: Monetary assertion operation semantics
bundles.description: The complete state-reading and state-changing operation surface of a monetary assertion bound to a host record: deterministic as-of resolution, binding and creation preconditions, correction by supersession, review and approval evidence, and disposition readiness. Every operation is declarative and produces a resolution, a check result, a plan, an evidence compilation or a readiness verdict.
bundles.rationale: A monetary assertion is only meaningful relative to a host, an effective time and a declared precision, so its operation contract cannot be inferred from the payload alone. Precision must survive round-trips (SRC-044), the currency reference must be resolved against the register list that applied at the effective instant (SRC-001), effective and observation time must be distinguished (SRC-027, SRC-017, SRC-048), concurrent change must be mediated by validators and preconditions (SRC-041, SRC-043), correction must be expressed as derivation and invalidation rather than mutation (SRC-034, SRC-045), and removal readiness must be reported separately from disposition execution (SRC-037, SRC-042). Authorization stays advisory because the decision belongs to a policy decision point (SRC-035, SRC-036), and every outcome — including failure — must be machine-identifiable (SRC-047).

layers.name: Read plane: effective-time resolution
layers.description: How a request selects exactly one version of a bound monetary assertion for a stated effective instant and observation cut-off, what it returns verbatim, and how it reports a non-result, a broken binding or a tombstone. Reads are safe: they change no state.

findings.name: Deterministic as-of read of a bound monetary assertion
findings.description: The rules that make a read reproducible: which two instants the caller supplies, which single version those instants select, what must be returned unchanged, and how an unresolvable, absent or retired result is reported. A monetary amount carries an explicit validity interval rather than an implied always-current value, so a read without an as-of pair is under-specified.

questions.text: Which effective instant and which observation cut-off instant does a read supply, and what is the declared default when either is omitted?
answer_data: Requested effective (valuation) instant as an RFC 3339 value with seconds and an explicit offset or Z
Requested observation/ingestion cut-off instant in the same form
Declared defaults, for example effective = request instant and observation = latest recorded
Statement of whether a caller-supplied offset is preserved or normalised, and which form is used for comparison

questions.text: Which single assertion version is selected when more than one effective interval covers the requested instant, and how is a tie broken?
answer_data: Ordered list of candidate versions with their effective intervals
Interval boundary convention (inclusive start, exclusive end) and the containment test applied
Deterministic tie-break key, for example latest observation instant then highest version counter
Explicit none-applicable outcome marker used instead of returning the nearest version

questions.text: Which stored values must a read return verbatim, and which derivations are forbidden in the read path?
answer_data: Amount returned as the stored canonical decimal string including trailing zeros, with the declared scale
Currency code returned as stored, plus the register list and status that applied at the effective instant
Prohibition on conversion, re-scaling, rounding or unit substitution during a read
Flag raised when the stored currency code is historic or withdrawn at the effective instant

questions.text: How does a read report an unresolvable host binding, a tombstoned assertion, or an as-of request outside the supported range?
answer_data: Structured failure descriptor with a resolvable type URI, title, status, detail and instance
Distinct codes for unknown identifier, unresolvable binding, tombstoned assertion and unsupported as-of window
Gone-style outcome for a tombstoned assertion, kept distinct from unknown-identifier
Reference to the advisory eligibility report when a value is withheld rather than absent

data_elements.name: Requested effective instant
data_elements.description: The valuation instant for which the caller wants the monetary assertion resolved.

data_elements.name: Requested observation cut-off instant
data_elements.description: The recording-time cut-off; versions recorded after this instant are excluded, allowing a past view of what was known at a given time.

data_elements.name: Version selection trace
data_elements.description: Ordered record of candidate versions considered, the containment test result for each, and the tie-break key applied, sufficient to reproduce the selection.

data_elements.name: Resolution outcome code
data_elements.description: Coded result of the read: resolved, none-applicable, unresolvable-binding, tombstoned or withheld.

data_elements.name: Currency register status at effective instant
data_elements.description: Which maintenance-agency list the referenced code belonged to at the effective instant: current currency, fund code or historic/withdrawn.

findings.inline_only_rationale: An as-of read is a deterministic projection computed over assertion versions the host already persists; it creates no new governed content. Emitting a stored artifact for every read would produce a second, divergent copy of a host-owned record and would imply ownership of persistence and of audit-trail production, both of which belong to the host and to the audit component respectively. The read therefore exists only as inline request parameters plus reference values — the selected version identifier, its validator, and the outcome code — with no artifact of its own.

layers.name: Change plane: binding, creation and correction
layers.description: How a monetary assertion is attached to a resolvable host anchor and created under explicit preconditions and idempotency, and how an erroneous or overtaken assertion is corrected by issuing a superseding version while the original stays immutable.

findings.name: Create and bind a monetary assertion to a resolvable host anchor
findings.description: The anchor that ties an assertion to one host record and attribute path, the preconditions that must hold before a create is accepted, the mechanism that distinguishes a retried request from a second assertion, and the references whose continued resolvability keeps the binding valid.

questions.text: Which resolvable identifier and attribute path anchor the assertion to its host, and how is that anchor demonstrated to resolve?
answer_data: Host master-system identifier and the host model or type it belongs to
Attribute path or role name the assertion occupies within the host
Resolver reference, resolution outcome and the observation instant of the resolution attempt
Cardinality rule stating whether the path admits one assertion or a series

questions.text: Which preconditions must hold before a create is accepted, and which of them are hard failures rather than warnings?
answer_data: Currency code present in the applicable maintenance-agency list at the effective instant
Declared scale consistent with the minor unit, or an explicit over-precision declaration with a stated reason
Host anchor resolves and is neither tombstoned nor under a blocking hold
Per-precondition severity classification and the aggregate accept/reject verdict

questions.text: How is a repeated create recognised as the same request rather than as a second assertion?
answer_data: Client-supplied idempotency key, its uniqueness scope and its published expiry policy
Request fingerprint computed over the canonical assertion payload
Replay behaviour returning the first recorded outcome, success or failure alike
Distinct outcomes for a duplicate arriving while the original is in flight and for key reuse with a different fingerprint

questions.text: Which outbound references must stay resolvable for the binding to remain valid, and what is reported when one of them breaks?
answer_data: Host anchor reference and its last successful resolution instant
Currency register entry reference and the list it was drawn from
References to the authorization context, retention class and any review record
Broken-reference report giving reference kind, failure mode, severity and whether reads remain permitted

data_elements.name: Host anchor reference
data_elements.description: Resolvable reference to the host record that carries the monetary assertion, expressed as the host's authoritative identifier plus its model reference.

data_elements.name: Host attribute path
data_elements.description: Named path or role within the host at which the assertion is bound, disambiguating multiple monetary attributes on one host.

data_elements.name: Request idempotency key
data_elements.description: Caller-supplied unique key identifying one logical create request across retries; must not be reused with a different payload.

data_elements.name: Canonical request fingerprint
data_elements.description: Digest over the canonical form of the submitted assertion payload, compared alongside the idempotency key to detect payload divergence.

data_elements.name: Precondition outcome entry
data_elements.description: One evaluated precondition with its identifier, verdict, severity, evidence reference and the observation instant of evaluation.

artifacts.name: Binding precondition and idempotency report
artifacts.description: Declarative record of every precondition evaluated for a create/bind request: the resolved host anchor, the currency register lookup, the scale/minor-unit consistency check, the idempotency key and fingerprint state, and the aggregate readiness verdict with a structured failure descriptor where applicable. It records findings only and performs no write.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the authoritative master-system report identifier issued by the host workflow system where one exists; otherwise a governed IRI minted in a namespace the adopting Dimension controls; otherwise a ULID minted by the adopting Dimension. The report carries its creation instant as content and is never identified by it.

findings.name: Correct a monetary assertion by supersession
findings.description: How a wrong or overtaken monetary assertion is replaced: a new version linked to the one it supersedes, the prior effective interval closed without gap or overlap, a current concurrency validator presented, and the original left byte-for-byte intact but marked invalid where appropriate.

questions.text: Which links connect a correcting version to the version it supersedes, and which agent and reason are recorded with it?
answer_data: Identifier and validator of the superseded version
Relation type distinguishing revision of the same assertion from derivation of a new one
Correction reason code plus free-text justification
Responsible agent reference and the activity that generated the new version, with its generation instant

questions.text: How is the effective interval of the superseded version closed, and how are gaps and overlaps across the version series detected?
answer_data: End instant applied to the prior interval and the boundary convention used
Overlap and gap test results across the whole series, expressed as interval relations
Retroactive flag set when the new interval begins before the current instant, with the reason
Rule for an open-ended final interval and how it is closed

questions.text: Which concurrency validator must a correction present, and what happens when the validator is stale?
answer_data: Current version validator or version counter obtained from the last read
Required conditional predicate that the change must carry
Stale-validator outcome code, whether it is reported as precondition failure or conflict, and the remediation instruction
Serialisation rule for two corrections targeting the same version

questions.text: Which parts of a superseded version may never be rewritten, and how is an unusable version marked without erasing it?
answer_data: Immutable fields of the original version: amount, currency, scale, effective interval and observation instant
Invalidation instant and coded invalidation reason
Status marker such as entered-in-error, withdrawn or superseded, with the marker's own observation instant
Explicit statement that correction never mutates the original payload and never reuses its identifier

data_elements.name: Superseded version reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the assertion version that this version replaces, together with that version's validator at the time the correction was planned.

data_elements.name: Version validator
data_elements.description: Opaque strong validator or monotonic version counter identifying the exact current state of the assertion, used as the concurrency token.

data_elements.name: Effective interval
data_elements.description: Begin and end instants during which the asserted amount is held to be valid, with the boundary convention declared; the end may be open.

data_elements.name: Correction reason code
data_elements.description: Coded reason for the supersession, distinguishing data error, late-arriving information, restatement and re-measurement instructed elsewhere.

data_elements.name: Invalidation instant
data_elements.description: Instant from which the superseded version is no longer usable for new decisions, recorded without deleting the version.

artifacts.name: Monetary assertion correction plan
artifacts.description: Declarative proposal naming the version to be superseded and its validator, the replacement amount, currency reference, scale and effective interval, the closure applied to the prior interval, the interval overlap/gap test results, the correction reason and agent, and the enumerated failure outcomes if the validator is stale. The host decides whether to apply it.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the authoritative master-system change-request identifier where the host issues one; otherwise a governed IRI in a Dimension-controlled namespace; otherwise a ULID minted by the adopting Dimension. Plan identifiers never embed an effective date, an amount or a currency code.

layers.name: Assurance plane: review evidence and disposition readiness
layers.description: What evidence must accompany a proposed monetary state change before it can be relied on, how eligibility is reported without deciding access, and how readiness for removal is assessed and handed to the parties that actually execute disposition.

findings.name: Review and approval evidence for a proposed monetary state change
findings.description: The evidence set that makes a proposed create, correction or disposition action reviewable: reviewer identity and asserted competence, the decision recorded, the securing proof and validity of the evidence, and an advisory eligibility statement that explicitly declines to decide access.

questions.text: Which evidence items must be present before a proposed monetary state change counts as reviewed?
answer_data: Reviewer identity reference and the role under which the review was performed
Review decision value and its decision instant
Reference to the precondition report or correction plan actually reviewed, pinned by digest
Supporting document references with integrity digests, and a named-gaps list where an item is missing

questions.text: Which authority is asserted to give the reviewer competence for this action, and where is that mandate recorded?
answer_data: Reference to the mandate, delegation or role assignment relied on
Scope limits of the mandate, including amount thresholds and currency or host restrictions
Validity interval of the mandate and its status reference
Pointer to the external register that holds the mandate, with a statement that this model does not confer it

questions.text: What does the eligibility report assert, and what does it explicitly decline to determine?
answer_data: Requested action and the target assertion version with its validator
Attributes supplied about subject, object, operation and environment
Advisory verdict drawn from eligible, not-eligible, indeterminate or not-applicable
Explicit statement that the external authorization component issues the binding permit or deny and that this report may be disregarded

questions.text: How is review evidence checked for currency and revocation before anyone relies on it?
answer_data: Evidence validity interval and whether the check instant falls inside it
Status or revocation list reference and the instant of the last successful status check
Verification outcome for the securing proof or digest
Aggregate completeness verdict listing every missing or stale item by name

data_elements.name: Reviewer reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the agent that performed a review, with the role asserted for the review and the instant of their decision.

data_elements.name: Review decision value
data_elements.description: Coded outcome of the review: approved, approved-with-conditions, rejected or returned-for-information.

data_elements.name: Asserted authority reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the external mandate or delegation relied on for the review, with its scope limits and validity interval.

data_elements.name: Advisory eligibility verdict
data_elements.description: Non-binding verdict about whether the requested action appears permissible, alongside the attributes supplied to the external decision point.

data_elements.name: Evidence status reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the revocation or status mechanism for a piece of review evidence, plus the instant of the last successful check.

artifacts.name: Monetary change review record
artifacts.description: Compiled evidence record for one proposed monetary state change: the reviewed plan or report pinned by digest, reviewer identities and asserted mandates, decision values and instants, evidence validity and status-check outcomes, the completeness verdict with named gaps, and the advisory eligibility statement with its explicit disclaimer of decision authority.
media_or_form: signed or otherwise secured evidence set
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the authoritative master-system review identifier from the governing workflow or case system where one exists; otherwise a governed IRI in a Dimension-controlled namespace; otherwise a UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension. Review instants are content, never identifier components.

findings.name: Deletion and tombstone readiness for a monetary assertion
findings.description: How readiness for removal is assessed and reported: which holds currently suspend disposition, which retention class governs and who owns it, what must survive as a tombstone so existing references stay interpretable, and which unresolved conditions block a verdict. Execution stays with the records authority and the host.

questions.text: Which holds or freezes currently suspend disposition of this assertion, and where does each one originate?
answer_data: Hold identifier, issuing authority reference and the instrument type relied on
Hold scope: whether it attaches to the assertion, the host record or a wider aggregate
Applied instant and lift instant where known, with the lift request reference
Effect statement recording that scheduled disposition is suspended until the hold is formally lifted

questions.text: Which retention class or records schedule governs this assertion, and which authority owns that schedule?
answer_data: Retention class or records-schedule reference and its version
Owning records authority reference and contact route
Retention trigger event and period as recorded by that authority, carried as a reference value
Explicit statement that this model neither sets, interprets nor executes the schedule

questions.text: What must remain after removal so that references from the host and from prior versions stay interpretable?
answer_data: Tombstone marker carrying the assertion identifier and version-series identifier
Removal instant and coded removal reason
Reference to the disposition authorisation relied on
Rule that the amount, the currency code and the effective interval values are not retained in the tombstone, and that the identifier is never reused

questions.text: Which unresolved conditions block a readiness verdict, and how is an incomplete assessment expressed?
answer_data: Blocker list typed as active hold, unresolved host reference, missing or stale schedule reference, or pending review
Per-blocker severity and the external owner responsible for clearing it
Aggregate verdict drawn from ready, blocked or indeterminate, never from a silent default
Re-evaluation instant and the structured failure descriptor for an unassessable assertion

data_elements.name: Applicable hold reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a hold or freeze that suspends scheduled disposition, with its issuing authority, scope and applied instant.

data_elements.name: Retention class reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the externally owned retention class or records schedule that governs the assertion, including its version.

data_elements.name: Tombstone marker
data_elements.description: Post-removal placeholder holding the assertion identifier, version-series identifier, removal instant, removal reason and disposition authorisation reference, and nothing of the monetary content.

data_elements.name: Disposition readiness verdict
data_elements.description: Aggregate assessment of whether the assertion is ready for disposition, blocked, or cannot be assessed, with the blocker list attached.

artifacts.name: Disposition readiness report
artifacts.description: Declarative report listing every hold in force, the referenced retention class and its owning authority, the reference-integrity results, the proposed tombstone content, the blocker list with owners and severities, and the aggregate verdict with a re-evaluation instant. It is an input to the records authority's decision and is never evidence that destruction occurred.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the authoritative master-system disposition-case identifier issued by the records authority where one exists; otherwise a governed IRI in a Dimension-controlled namespace; otherwise a ULID minted by the adopting Dimension. Report identifiers never encode a retention date or a removal instant.

bundles.name: Monetary calculation, reconciliation and projection operations
bundles.description: The operation surface that turns a stored monetary value into a defensible computed, compared or published result: admissibility validation, quantisation, valuation and conversion with lineage, reconciliation against tolerance, and lossy or redacted export.
bundles.rationale: Monetary correctness fails at the operation boundary, not at the field boundary. Standards fix the code list and the amount shape, but the reproducibility of a derived value depends on which rate, which reference time, which rounding policy and which tolerance were bound — and on whether the original amount and currency survived the derivation. Grouping these as one bundle keeps arithmetic, provenance and outcome semantics under a single contract while leaving rate acquisition, posting, persistence and authorisation to their owners.

layers.name: Admission and quantisation
layers.description: Whether a monetary value may enter a calculation at all, and how it is brought to a target scale without silently losing or inventing value.

findings.name: Monetary value admissibility
findings.description: The checks a monetary value must pass before any downstream calculation: the currency identifier resolves in the referenced register and has a status permitting the requested operation; the amount is an exact decimal rather than a binary floating-point approximation; the declared scale, digit limits and allowed currency set of the caller-pinned profile are satisfied; and the measurement basis and valuation instant are present. Failure produces a typed outcome rather than a coerced value.

questions.text: Which admissibility checks must a monetary value pass before any downstream calculation is attempted?
answer_data: currency identifier resolvable in the referenced register version
amount represented as an exact decimal with a declared scale
scale not exceeding the profile digit limits
valuation instant present with an explicit offset

questions.text: How is an unsupported, historic, fund or non-transactional currency identifier distinguished from an active transactional currency?
Which profile-specific constraints — allowed currency set, maximum total digits, maximum fraction digits and amount bounds — apply to the calling context?
What outcome is emitted when a value is inadmissible, and does that outcome block the operation or degrade it?
answer_data: outcome code from the model taxonomy

data_elements.name: Currency identifier
data_elements.description: The identifier of the currency in which the amount is denominated, resolved against a named register version rather than copied.

data_elements.name: Exact decimal amount
data_elements.description: The amount as an exact decimal value with an explicitly declared scale; binary floating-point representation is inadmissible because it cannot represent common minor-unit fractions exactly.

data_elements.name: Currency status
data_elements.description: The status of the currency identifier in the referenced register version, distinguishing active, fund, historic and replaced codes and the operations each permits.

data_elements.name: Validation profile pin
data_elements.description: Reference to the caller-pinned validation profile and its version, which supplies allowed currencies, digit limits and amount bounds for the context.

data_elements.name: Validation outcome
data_elements.description: Typed outcome codes emitted by admissibility evaluation, including unsupported currency, non-transactional code status, scale exceeded and missing measurement basis.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Admissibility evaluation yields a transient predicate result carried inline in the operation response alongside the value it describes. It has no independent identity, no lifecycle and no distribution of its own: the same value re-validated against a different profile yields a different result, so a stored validation object would be misleading rather than authoritative. The durable evidence record, if the adopting Dimension needs one, is created and retained by the referenced audit or records system, whose evidence and audit-trail semantics this model does not own.

findings.name: Quantisation, rounding policy and residual
findings.description: How an exact amount is brought to a target scale: the target scale (usually but not always the currency minor unit), the rounding mode and tie-breaking rule, the resulting residual, and how a residual is allocated when a total is split across components so that the parts still sum to the whole. Precision loss is an explicit, declared outcome rather than an invisible side effect.

questions.text: What rounding policy — target scale, rounding mode and tie-breaking rule — governs quantisation of this amount?
answer_data: order of quantisation relative to other operations

questions.text: What residual arises from quantisation, and how is it computed, reported or allocated across components?
When may the target scale differ from the currency minor unit, and which authority pins that deviation?
answer_data: scope in which the deviation is valid

questions.text: How is precision loss detected and expressed so that a consumer knows the value is no longer exact?

data_elements.name: Declared scale
data_elements.description: The number of fractional digits to which the amount is stated, which may equal the currency minor unit or a pinned deviation from it.

data_elements.name: Rounding mode and tie rule
data_elements.description: The rounding mode applied and the tie-breaking rule used when a value falls exactly half-way, stated explicitly because regimes differ.

data_elements.name: Quantisation residual
data_elements.description: The signed difference between the exact input amount and the quantised result, expressed in the same currency.

data_elements.name: Implied value interval
data_elements.description: The interval of plausible source values implied by the declared decimals and rounding mode of a quantised amount, used later for tolerance evaluation.

data_elements.name: Exactness indicator
data_elements.description: Whether the stated amount is exact or the product of a lossy quantisation.

artifacts.name: Rounding policy profile
artifacts.description: A declarative, versioned profile stating target scale rules per currency or context, rounding mode, tie-breaking rule, residual allocation method and the order of quantisation relative to conversion. It is referenced by derivations so that a historical result remains reproducible after the policy changes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative identifier issued by the adopting Dimension's policy registry plus an immutable version identifier; where no registry identifier exists, a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. The effective-from instant is an attribute, never the identifier.

artifacts.name: Quantisation record
artifacts.description: The reportable result of one quantisation: exact input amount and currency, target scale, applied policy profile reference, quantised output, signed residual, exactness indicator and implied value interval.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identifier of the operation invocation supplied by the caller if it has one; otherwise a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, bound to the content hash of the input amount, policy reference and output.

layers.name: Valuation and conversion
layers.description: How a monetary value is restated in another currency or measurement basis using an externally supplied rate binding, and what lineage must travel with the result so it can be reproduced or refuted.

findings.name: Rate binding, conversion arithmetic and derivation lineage
findings.description: The complete binding needed to make a conversion reproducible: which rate source and publication supplied the rate, the base and quote currencies and quotation direction, the reference time the rate represents versus the instant it was retrieved, any intermediate leg in a rate chain, the measurement basis of the result, the intermediate precision and the point at which quantisation is applied. The derived value always carries the original amount and currency; it never replaces them.

questions.text: Which rate source, publication and retrieval act produced the rate used for this derivation?
How are base and quote currencies, quotation direction and any intermediate leg expressed so the computation can be reproduced exactly?
answer_data: rate value with its own significant figures
ordered rate chain legs and pivot currency

questions.text: Which reference time governs rate selection, and how does it differ from the valuation instant and the retrieval instant?
answer_data: reference-time selector (transaction date, measurement date, period-pinned rate)

questions.text: What arithmetic rules constrain the computation: multiplication versus division, permissibility of an inverse rate, intermediate scale and the order of quantisation?
answer_data: inverse-rate permission flag and its authority
significant figures retained in the rate
order of quantisation relative to chaining

data_elements.name: Original amount and currency
data_elements.description: The unmodified source amount and currency retained on every derived value, so that a derivation can always be re-run or reversed.

data_elements.name: Rate source reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the external publisher, dataset and publication instance that supplied the rate, together with any stated fitness-for-purpose limitation.

data_elements.name: Rate value and direction
data_elements.description: The rate as published, with base currency, quote currency, quotation direction and the significant figures in which it was published.

data_elements.name: Rate reference instant
data_elements.description: The instant the rate is deemed to represent, distinct from the instant it was retrieved.

data_elements.name: Rate retrieval instant
data_elements.description: The instant at which the rate was obtained by the calling system, recorded separately to expose staleness.

data_elements.name: Rate chain
data_elements.description: The ordered sequence of legs, including any pivot currency, when no direct rate exists between base and quote currency.

data_elements.name: Measurement basis
data_elements.description: The basis on which the value is measured, such as historical cost at transaction date, closing-rate restatement, or a fair value measured at a stated measurement date.

data_elements.name: Derivation outcome
data_elements.description: Typed outcome codes for conversion, including rate missing, rate stale beyond threshold, ambiguous rate among several published rates, currency not exchangeable, invalid or prohibited inverse, zero or non-positive rate, and precision loss.

artifacts.name: Derivation record
artifacts.description: The self-contained lineage object that accompanies a derived monetary value: original amount and currency, rate binding with direction and chain, rate reference and retrieval instants, measurement basis, applied rounding policy reference, intermediate values, residual, final quantised result and any outcome codes. A third party holding only this record can recompute the result.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system derivation identifier where the calling system issues one; otherwise a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, bound to a content hash over original value, rate binding, reference instant and policy reference. The valuation date is an attribute, never the identifier.

artifacts.name: Rate binding
artifacts.description: The reusable, citable statement of which rate applies for a given currency pair, reference time and policy context, including the source reference, direction, published significant figures, staleness threshold and permitted use. It is consumed as input; this model does not produce or publish rates.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identifier assigned by the external rate publisher or the adopting Dimension's rate catalogue; failing that, a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, qualified by the source reference and reference instant as attributes.

layers.name: Reconciliation and projection
layers.description: How derived and stated monetary values are checked against one another within a declared tolerance, and how they are projected outward — including deliberately lossy, rounded, banded or suppressed forms.

findings.name: Reconciliation against declared tolerance
findings.description: Comparison of a set of monetary values — components against a total, a restated value against an independently stated one, or a computed balance against a reported balance — where comparability requires the same currency, compatible measurement bases and a stated reference time. Tolerance is derived from declared precision intervals, an absolute band or a relative band, and is always declared, never assumed. Outside-tolerance difference is a reportable outcome with attribution, not an error to be absorbed.

questions.text: What tolerance applies to this reconciliation, and is it derived from declared decimals, an absolute band or a relative band?
answer_data: tolerance value or interval derivation rule
rounding mode assumed by the interval

questions.text: Which values form the reconciliation set, and on what basis are they comparable to each other?
What is emitted when the difference falls outside tolerance, and how is the unexplained residual attributed?
answer_data: attribution to quantisation, rate binding or missing member

questions.text: What must accompany a reconciliation result so that an independent party can recompute the same verdict?
answer_data: input value references with declared decimals
derivation record references for restated members

data_elements.name: Reconciliation set
data_elements.description: The ordered set of member monetary values with their roles and signed weights that participate in a single reconciliation.

data_elements.name: Tolerance declaration
data_elements.description: The declared basis and value of the permitted difference, including whether it is derived from precision intervals, an absolute band or a relative band.

data_elements.name: Reconciliation difference
data_elements.description: The signed difference between the reported and computed totals, expressed in the common currency of the set.

data_elements.name: Reconciliation verdict
data_elements.description: The typed verdict of the comparison: consistent within tolerance, outside tolerance, or not evaluable because members are incomparable or incomplete.

data_elements.name: Difference attribution
data_elements.description: Decomposition of the difference into explained causes such as quantisation residual, differing rate binding or differing measurement basis, plus the unexplained remainder.

artifacts.name: Reconciliation statement
artifacts.description: The reportable output of one reconciliation run: the member set with declared decimals, the tolerance declaration and its basis, the computed and reported totals, the signed difference, the verdict and the attribution of the difference. It reports; it does not correct, post or approve.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system run identifier issued by the calling reconciliation process where one exists; otherwise a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, with the run sequence number and period as attributes rather than identifier components.

findings.name: Projection, lossy export and redaction
findings.description: Projection of a monetary value into a target representation — a message field, a reporting fact, a tabular cell or a display string — and the deliberate degradation of that projection through scaling, banding, rounding or suppression. The projection declares its own losses: whether the exported value is exact, rounded to a coarser scale, an interval, or suppressed; whether it remains reconcilable; and under which external authorisation any redaction was applied.

questions.text: Into which target representation is the value projected, and how are amount, currency and precision mapped without changing meaning?
Which redaction or generalisation operations are applied to the projected value, and which authorisation decision directed them?
answer_data: operation applied (suppression, banding, controlled rounding, interval publication)

questions.text: How does the projection declare that it is lossy, non-reconcilable or partially suppressed?
answer_data: declared decimals or interval of the exported value

questions.text: How long may a projection be treated as current, and what marks it as superseded by a newer derivation?

data_elements.name: Projection target
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the target representation into which the monetary value is mapped.

data_elements.name: Applied scale factor
data_elements.description: Any presentation scaling applied to the exported amount, such as thousands or millions, recorded so the underlying magnitude remains recoverable.

data_elements.name: Redaction operation
data_elements.description: The disclosure-protection operation applied to the projected value, such as primary or secondary suppression, controlled or random rounding, or publication as an interval.

data_elements.name: Authorisation decision reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the externally made authorisation or disclosure decision that directed the redaction; this model carries the reference and never makes the decision.

data_elements.name: Lossiness declaration
data_elements.description: Explicit statement of whether the projected value is exact, rounded, banded or suppressed, and whether it can still participate in reconciliation.

artifacts.name: Projection manifest
artifacts.description: The declaration accompanying an exported set of monetary values: target representation and version, field mappings, applied scale factor, per-value lossiness and reconcilability indicators, redaction operations with their authorisation references, and the derivation records behind any restated value.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Export identifier issued by the master system performing the export where one exists; otherwise a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, bound to a content hash of the projected value set. The export date is an attribute, never the identifier.

functions.name: Parse and normalize an exact decimal amount
functions.description: Accepts an amount as a decimal lexical token or as an explicit coefficient-and-scale pair, and produces a normalized sign, coefficient and scale together with the canonical lexical form. Rejects any input that cannot be held exactly at the declared scale; it never rounds silently and never accepts a binary floating-point source as authoritative.
inputs: Amount as a decimal lexical token or as an explicit coefficient-and-scale pair
Declared scale for the host field
Total-digit and fraction-digit bounds in force
Negative-zero policy
outputs: Normalized sign, coefficient and scale
Canonical lexical form of the amount
Parse and validation diagnostics
preconditions: The input is a decimal lexical form or an exact coefficient-and-scale pair, not a binary floating-point value
The declared scale and digit bounds are supplied by the host or profile
The negative-zero policy is declared where a signed zero can occur
effects: Rejects an input that is not exactly representable at the declared scale and records the reason
Preserves the declared scale so that trailing-zero significance is not lost
Produces a canonical form suitable for storage, hashing and equality
Performs no rounding, no arithmetic and no currency conversion

functions.name: Validate the currency reference against the pinned catalogue edition
functions.description: Resolves the declared currency code against the pinned, integrity-verified catalogue snapshot and reports the entry's class, status and published minor unit, or reports the code as unresolved. Catalogue identifier, list designator and pinned published edition
Integrity digest of the retained catalogue snapshot
Set of code classes the host field permits
outputs: Resolution status for the code
Resolved code class and status as at the pinned edition
Published minor unit value or an explicit not-applicable flag
Mismatch and unresolved diagnostics

The catalogue and list the code belongs to are declared on the reference
The host has declared which code classes it accepts

Reports disagreement between the alphabetic and numeric forms without choosing one silently
Forces an explicit host-declared scale when the catalogue publishes no applicable minor unit
Makes no change to catalogue content and no assertion about jurisdiction, legal tender or exchangeability

functions.name: Determine the declared value determinacy state
functions.description: Inspects a monetary declaration and reports whether it asserts an exact point value, an interval, an approximate value or an explicit absence with a reason, flagging contradictory combinations. Declared determinacy-state vocabulary
Declared absent-reason vocabulary
Interval endpoints where present

Absent reason where the declaration asserts no amount
Interval endpoint set with inclusivity flags
Contradiction diagnostics

Interval endpoints, where present, each carry a currency reference and a declared scale

Flags a declaration that simultaneously asserts an amount and an absence
Flags interval endpoints whose currency references or scales disagree

functions.description: Compares two exact point declarations that resolve to the same currency code under the same catalogue, returning an ordering or equality result. Externally supplied policy-compatibility assertion
Trailing-zero significance policy to apply to equality

Reason code when comparison is refused
Statement of the equality semantics applied

Both currency references resolve to the same code under the same catalogue and pinned edition
A policy-compatibility assertion is supplied by the caller

Refuses comparison when the external compatibility assertion is missing
Distinguishes numeric equality from representational identity according to the trailing-zero policy
Performs no currency conversion, no rate lookup and no arithmetic beyond comparison

currency precision profile snapshot reference
exchange-profile digit limits where a profile is named

defect list naming the declaration element at fault for each unmet requirement
resolved effective policy view for the caller

the policy declares an effective-from timestamp

allocation rule reference and version

residual assignment target

Valuation instant with seconds and offset, plus temporal kind
Measurement basis code and defining authority reference
Market, session or scenario reference

Completeness report listing any missing mandatory context
Ingestion instant recorded separately from the valuation instant

All referenced classifier schemes resolve to a concrete version

functions.name: Select a declared rate under a caller-supplied policy

Valuation instant and required effective coverage
