composition.purpose: The assertion is mixed into a host record at a named attribute path. The host owns its own identifiers, its own lifecycle, persistence and enforcement; this model supplies the anchor, the version series, the operation preconditions and the reports. No host lifecycle state is defined here.

composition.target: ISO 4217 currency and funds register (ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency lists One, Two and Three)
composition.purpose: Alphabetic codes, numeric codes and minor units are referenced from the register together with the list and status that applied at the effective instant. Allocation, amendment, redenomination and withdrawal of codes remain wholly with the maintenance agency.

composition.target: External authorization component (policy decision point and policy enforcement point)
composition.purpose: This model supplies attributes and emits advisory eligibility statements. The decision point renders the authoritative Permit, Deny, Indeterminate or NotApplicable outcome and the enforcement point enforces it, including any obligations. No evaluation, decision or enforcement semantics are owned locally.

composition.target: Records authority, retention schedule and disposition programme
composition.purpose: Retention classes, disposition authorities, holds and physical destruction are authored, decided and executed by the records authority. This model carries the references and reports readiness only; it never schedules, approves or performs disposition.

composition.target: Audit trail and event log model
composition.purpose: Operation attempts and outcomes are captured, secured and retained by the audit component. This model emits correlation references so an outcome can be reconciled with an audit entry, and owns no audit-trail production, retention or tamper-evidence semantics.

composition.target: Foreign-exchange rate observation and conversion model
composition.purpose: Rate feeds, rate selection, spot and closing rate policy and conversion arithmetic live in that model. A converted amount is a separate monetary assertion produced there and referenced here; no operation in this model derives one.

composition.target: W3C PROV-O provenance vocabulary
composition.purpose: Supersession, derivation, responsible agent, generation instant and invalidation instant are expressed as mappings to PROV terms. The alignment is a mapping claim for interoperability; no conformance to PROV-O is asserted and no PROV processing behaviour is adopted.

composition.target: Monetary payload types: HL7 FHIR Money and XBRL monetary items with ISO 4217 unit measures
composition.purpose: Amount plus currency reference with preserved precision is mapped to established payload types for exchange, including the instant-versus-duration period distinction. Field-level differences, especially permitted fraction digits, are recorded as conflicts rather than reconciled by assumption.

composition.target: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0
composition.purpose: Review and approval evidence may be carried as verifiable credentials with a validity interval, a status reference and a securing proof. Issuance, verification, presentation and status-list operation stay with the issuer, holder and verifier; this model only compiles and checks what it is given.

composition.target: WM-ECO-004
composition.purpose: Registered parent economic model that supplies the surrounding economic-value context; WM-XCT-032 contributes only the monetary value structure and its calculation, reconciliation and projection semantics.

composition.target: Host entity, event or agreement models that carry monetary attributes
composition.purpose: Attach amount, currency, measurement basis, valuation instant, declared precision and derivation lineage to any host record without the host redefining monetary arithmetic.

composition.target: Currency register maintained under ISO 4217 by its maintenance agency
composition.purpose: Resolve currency identifiers, numeric codes, minor units and code status against the governing register version; the register's assignment, amendment and withdrawal lifecycle stays with the maintenance agency.

composition.target: External exchange-rate source or market data service
composition.purpose: Consume a rate binding as an input and record its source, publication reference, reference instant and retrieval instant; rate acquisition, publication schedules, suspension of pairs and fitness-for-purpose statements remain owned by the publisher.

composition.target: Accounting policy, recognition and ledger posting model
composition.purpose: Carry the measurement basis and reference-time selector that an accounting policy dictates, and hand computed values back for recognition; selection of the applicable rate policy, recognition of exchange differences and posting remain external.

composition.target: Payment message and scheme profile models
composition.purpose: Constrain validation profiles to scheme and message-level currency and digit limits when a caller pins one, and preserve amount and currency meaning end to end across message projections.

composition.target: Business reporting fact model (XBRL / Open Information Model)
composition.purpose: Reuse declared-decimals, value-interval and calculation-consistency semantics for quantisation and reconciliation tolerance; taxonomies, contexts, dimensional models and filing rules remain in the reporting framework.

composition.target: Authorisation, disclosure-control and policy decision service
composition.purpose: Receive an authorisation decision reference and a redaction directive as inputs to a redaction operation; evaluation, enforcement and the audit trail of the decision are owned entirely by that service.

composition.target: Temporal representation model based on RFC 3339
composition.purpose: Express valuation instant, rate reference instant, retrieval instant and projection instant with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, so that staleness and supersession are computable.

composition.target: Currency-regime and jurisdictional conversion rule sets
composition.purpose: Specialise only the monetary computation parameters that a jurisdictional regime fixes — significant figures retained in a rate, permissibility of inverse rates, mandatory pivot currency, intermediate rounding depth and final rounding rule — without duplicating the regime's own legal authority, applicability or enforcement machinery.

composition.target: Records retention, storage and audit record systems
composition.purpose: Delegate persistence, retention scheduling, legal hold, erasure execution and audit-trail construction for monetary records and derivation lineage; this model defines disposition semantics only.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names an owner package that holds the model specification, the pinned currency code-list edition reference and the governing rounding, rate-source and profile policy references, and publishes their version labels.

The owner package declares which external components own authorization decisions, records disposition and audit records, and records those bindings as resolvable references before the model is used in production.

The owner package publishes the identifier scheme used for Dimension-assigned surrogate identifiers and the party register that role references resolve against, and states that role assertions are advisory.
The owner package records the regional and accounting profiles in force, including competing rate-source mandates, and the precedence rule or the decision to carry dual values.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Local identifiers are lower-kebab-case and prefixed for this model; they must not embed dates, amounts or currency codes. External vocabularies are referenced by their own governed identifiers - ISO 4217 codes by the maintenance agency's code with the list edition pinned, provenance terms by the PROV namespace IRI - and are never re-minted in a local namespace. Where a Dimension must mint an identifier, it uses a UUID or ULID under a namespace it controls and records the minting reason.
registry_links: Vercy registry entry vr.wm-xct-032 (model WM-XCT-032), parent WM-ECO-004
ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency currency code lists (current, fund and historic) as the referenced register
W3C PROV namespace http://www.w3.org/ns/prov# as the provenance alignment target

canonicalization_rules: Timestamps are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds present and an explicit numeric offset or Z; -00:00 is preserved as meaning an unknown local offset and is never rewritten to Z.

Currency codes are canonicalised to the uppercase alphabetic code with the numeric code carried alongside, and the code-list edition and amendment that resolved them are pinned rather than assumed current.
References are canonicalised to their authoritative identifier form; display names, labels and human-readable notes are excluded from any canonical form used for digests.
Digest inputs are canonicalised by sorting object keys, omitting absent optional fields and excluding the digest field itself, so that recomputation is deterministic across projections.
patch_rules: A change to amount, currency, applied rate, measurement basis or effective interval is a superseding version that cites the prior version and a change authority; where non-rewriteable preservation or an audit-trail alternative applies, in-place overwriting is prohibited.

A change to advisory metadata (handling labels, non-normative notes, mapping documentation) may be applied in place, and the recorded-at timestamp is updated while the effective interval is left unchanged.
A patch must not alter a pinned code-list edition, amendment number or policy version retroactively; re-pinning is recorded as a new assertion version with its own recorded-at time.
A patch that removes a field required by a governing profile is rejected and reported rather than applied silently.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional field, a new sensitivity class value or a new mapping entry is backward compatible; consumers ignore unknown optional fields.

Narrowing a cardinality, making an optional field required, or changing the meaning of a status or class code is breaking and requires a new model version and a re-issued profile conformance statement.
Historic currency codes remain valid in stored assertions after the register withdraws them; consumers must resolve them against the historic list rather than reject them.
A conformance claim against an external representation is invalidated when that representation's version changes and reverts to an alignment until the declared checks are re-run.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: the identifier issued by the system of record that owns the artifact or the host record it belongs to (for example the accounting or document system's record key), used whenever it exists and is stable.

Governed global identifier or IRI: an identifier from a governed external scheme, such as a maintenance-agency currency code with its pinned list edition or a namespace IRI, used where the artifact references externally governed content.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, minted only when neither of the above exists, with the minting reason recorded.

Composite weak key of host reference, role on host, currency and valuation context, used for resolution and collision detection but never as a substitute for a stable identifier when one is available.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are written in RFC 3339 form with seconds always present and an explicit numeric offset or Z; -00:00 is reserved for an unknown local offset and is not equivalent to Z. Event time and observation or ingestion time are recorded separately whenever they can differ: the valuation or measurement instant and the rate reference instant are event times, while the rate retrieval time, the recorded-at time and any digest computation time are observation or ingestion times. A date without a time of day may be recorded only where the governing profile defines the value as a whole-day event, and a date is never used as an identifier.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named by their stable parent key followed by a zero-padded monotonic sequence number that carries no date, amount or currency component - revision notes as assertion key plus revision sequence, and rate evidence snapshots as rate source and series plus the rate reference instant plus a capture sequence for repeated captures. Sequence numbers are never reused after supersession or disposal.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact records a digest value, the algorithm used and the digest computation time in an integrity manifest, computed over the canonical form. Corrections are additive superseding versions rather than edits, so that a modification history remains reconstructable where non-rewriteable preservation or an audit-trail alternative is required. Verification reports discrepancies only; it never repairs, quarantines or deletes evidence, and it is not a substitute for audit testing.

policies: Role, authority and segregation declarations are advisory metadata. An external authorization component owns every allow or deny decision, and no monetary value is presumed to have an owner or a valuation authority unless one is declared.

Lifecycle verbs in this model act on the monetary binding on its host. They never create or imply a lifecycle for a currency, a price, a rate feed, a transaction, an account or an instrument; where such a change is the cause, an external record is cited instead.

Rate and valuation inputs are recorded with their source, reference instant, retrieval time and any publisher-stated usage limitation; a rate published for information purposes only is never presented as a transaction rate.
Pinned references govern interpretation. A stored assertion is read against the code-list edition and policy versions pinned at assertion time, not against the current ones.

Conformance to an external standard is claimed only where declared checks have been run and evidenced; otherwise the relationship is recorded as an alignment, and known conflicts are recorded rather than reconciled by assumption.

read: Reads resolve the effective assertion for a host reference, role and point in time, returning the version whose effective interval covers that point together with its status and any superseding version.
Reads return pinned code-list and policy versions alongside the value so that a consumer can interpret a historic currency code or a superseded rounding policy correctly.

Reads of restricted values return the published attribute set and any declared projection constraint; the decision to release, mask or band the value is made and applied by the external authorization component.
Reads never mutate status, hold flags or retention state, and read access to preserved records must remain available to an entitled examiner for the duration of the retention period.
create: Creation requires a resolvable host reference and a role on host; a monetary assertion is never created without a host.
Creation records the recorded-at time and, where the value is derived, the original value reference, derivation activity, applied rate, rate reference instant and rate retrieval time.
Creation pins the currency code-list edition and amendment and the governing rounding, rate-source and profile policy versions, or records a content digest where the source publishes no version.
Creation may record advisory role assignments and a sensitivity class; absence of an owner or approver is represented explicitly rather than defaulted.
update: A change to amount, currency, applied rate, measurement basis or effective interval creates a superseding version citing the prior version, a change authority and, where applicable, the external record that triggered it.
In-place modification is prohibited wherever non-rewriteable preservation or an audit-trail alternative applies; the modification history must remain reconstructable.
Advisory metadata may be updated in place with a refreshed recorded-at timestamp, leaving the effective interval and pins untouched.
An update that would violate a pinned policy version or remove a profile-required field is rejected and reported, not silently coerced.
delete: Records of this model are never hard-deleted while their declared retention period is unexpired or a legal hold flag is active; the hold suppresses disposition until the issuing authority releases it.

On expiry of the retention period with no active hold, the record becomes disposition-eligible and is reduced to a tombstone that preserves the assertion key, host reference, currency code, retention class, disposition time and disposition record reference, while the amount, lineage detail and evidence content are irreversibly removed.
The tombstone retains the original assertion key so that inbound references resolve to a disposed marker rather than dangling; keys are never reused.

Execution of disposal, transfer and physical destruction, and the disposition record evidencing it, are owned by the adopting Dimension's records management authority under its retention schedule and by the applicable preservation rule for financial records. This model only assesses readiness, declares the tombstone content and stores the reference to the externally produced disposition record.
Where the host record's retention period is longer than the assertion's, the longer period governs and the record remains undeletable until the reconciled eligible-from time.

roles.name: Accountable value owner
responsibilities: Is recorded as accountable for a monetary value on its host and for the correctness of its declared context
Confirms the governing profile and the sensitivity class applied to the value
Requests correction through the declared change authority rather than editing a preserved value

roles.name: Currency-data steward
responsibilities: Maintains the pinned currency code-list edition and amendment reference and the handling of historic, fund and replaced codes
Maintains the rounding and minor-unit policy reference and its version label
Reports drift between pinned and currently published register content without amending stored assertions retroactively

roles.name: Valuation authority
responsibilities: Names the rate source and measurement basis permitted for a class of values under a profile
Records the fallback basis when a mandated source publishes nothing or a currency is not exchangeable
Records the publisher-stated usage limitations that must travel with a cited rate

roles.name: Preparer
responsibilities: Creates the monetary assertion with its host binding, valuation context, lineage fields and pins
Attaches the supporting evidence items and their digests
Declares explicitly where required context is unavailable rather than defaulting it

roles.name: Independent reviewer
responsibilities: Checks the assertion against its governing profile, pins and lineage completeness
Records the review outcome as an observable state and the evidence relied on, distinguishing automated checks from re-performance
Records a segregation relief declaration and compensating measure where positions overlap

roles.name: Approver
responsibilities: Records approval of the assertion or of a superseding correction under a cited change authority
Confirms that the correction mode complies with the applicable preservation rule
Does not act as preparer for the same assertion unless an unexpired relief declaration is recorded

roles.name: Records custodian
responsibilities: Maintains the retention class, trigger and hold flags for monetary context records and their evidence
Consumes disposition readiness reports and links the externally produced disposition record
Ensures preserved records remain accessible to entitled examiners for the retention period

roles.name: Access administrator
responsibilities: Maintains the mapping from sensitivity class and restriction basis to the attributes published for the external decision point
Registers time-bounded access exception declarations and their bases
Confirms that this model publishes attributes only and holds no decision or enforcement logic

access.default_rule: Deny by default at every scope. This model publishes object attributes, declared scopes and projection constraints; an external policy decision point evaluates each request against subject, resource, action and environment attributes, and an enforcement point applies the result and discharges any obligation. Nothing recorded here grants access by itself.
exceptions: Regulatory or supervisory examination access to preserved monetary records and their evidence, recorded as a time-bounded exception citing the preservation rule that requires ready accessibility.
External auditor access to evidence items and approval records for a defined engagement period, recorded with the engagement reference and an explicit non-transfer condition.
Counterparty-facing disclosure of a commercially restricted amount only where the restricting agreement permits it, with the permitted recipient class and interval recorded.
Break-glass access under a named authority, recorded with the requesting party, the justification, the interval and a mandatory post-hoc review reference.
Artifact-scope exception for a tombstone record, which remains resolvable after disposal because it carries no amount or evidence content.
audit_requirements: Each declared access exception records its basis reference, beneficiary class, interval and the party that registered it, so that the declaration itself is reviewable.
Attribute changes affecting release - sensitivity class, restriction basis, handling labels - are versioned with a recorded-at timestamp and the party that made them.

This model records references to externally held access and audit logs and their scope limitations; it does not store, evaluate or interpret the access log or the audit trail, which remain owned by the authorization and audit components.
Where an access exception expires or is released, the release time is recorded rather than the declaration being deleted, so the historical basis stays reconstructable.

required_fields: Pinned currency code-list edition and governing policy versions
Externally owned components: authorization decision point, records disposition authority, audit record source
Boundary statement: advisory roles only, no enforcement, no external lifecycle ownership
read_order: Read AGENTS.md first to obtain Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before any other artifact.
Read the Specification URL to load the model boundary, in-scope and out-of-scope statements and the boundary notes, so that target-owned concepts are not re-implemented locally.

Read the Storage type URL to learn how the format-neutral structure is projected into the concrete store, then the Interface URL for the read, create, update and delete contracts including the tombstone rule.
Read the Processes URL for the declarative check functions, then resolve the pinned currency code-list edition and policy versions before creating or interpreting any monetary assertion.

Resolve the externally owned components last and confirm their bindings; if the authorization decision point or the records disposition authority cannot be resolved, operate in read-only mode and report the gap.

coverage.claim: This audit reviewed all 11 bundles, 25 layers, 47 findings, 199 questions, 26 declared artifacts and 37 functions in the single Claude pass against its own scope statement, boundary notes, known_omissions, conflicts and adversarial_checks logs. It verifies internal consistency and self-declared boundaries only; it cannot confirm live source URLs or current version/edition labels, and it does not substitute for the still-pending second-provider or registry-level boundary review.

checklist.notes: Currency identity is a code plus catalogue plus pinned edition plus list designator; alphabetic and numeric forms are both carried, and symbols are excluded from identity on explicit CLDR evidence. Declaration identity derives from the host record and field path, with a Dimension-assigned identifier only as a last resort.

Nine candidate composition links describe the parent model, the code register, the host mix-in, decimal and schema alignments, message-type alignment, locale display, absent-value vocabulary and exchange-rate publication, each stating what remains with the target. The frozen relationship contract is empty, so these links remain pending registry confirmation.

Lifecycle verbs act only on the monetary binding on its host - asserted, revised, superseded, withdrawn - with correction-by-supersession where non-rewriteable preservation applies. No lifecycle is created for a currency, rate feed, transaction, account or instrument.

Effective interval, valuation and rate reference instants (event time) are separated from rate retrieval, recorded-at and digest computation times (observation time); all use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset, and -00:00 retains its distinct meaning.
Original-versus-derived lineage, derivation activity, applied rate and instant, agent attribution and delegation are aligned to PROV terms; a recomputation tolerance is declared.
Accountable value owner, currency-data steward and valuation authority are advisory and optional; no source supports a universal owner, so absence is represented explicitly rather than defaulted.
Attribute-only contribution with deny-by-default, four declared scopes and time-bounded exceptions; decision, enforcement and obligation discharge are explicitly outside the model.

Retention class and trigger, legal-hold suppression, disposition readiness assessment, tombstone content and key preservation are declared; disposal execution and the disposition record are owned by the records authority and the applicable preservation rule.
Profile declaration, mapping entries labelled alignment or conformance, declared losses, historic-code interpretation and precedence between competing rate mandates are all represented.

Declared scale and precision are separated from observed digits and from exponent normalisation. Minor units are version-pinned currency properties covering zero, two, three and four digits and the not-applicable case; profile digit limits are recorded as a separate constraint.
Mode, target exponent or increment, direction, tie handling, stage and channel scope are all required before a rule is interpretable; no default is supplied and an unnamed rule is a failure.

A compatibility gate over currency, valuation and rounding context precedes equality, ordering and aggregation; equality semantics must be selected explicitly; implicit conversion and re-quantization are prohibited and refusals are typed.

Named arithmetic conditions including invalid-operation, overflow, underflow, inexact, rounded, clamped and subnormal are surfaced by name; silent truncation, clamping and binary-float coercion are prohibited.

Bounded and estimated monetary values are declared with lower and upper bounds and a derivation method, but no primary monetary-specific source was found that governs how such bounds are derived or propagated. The structure records the bounds without prescribing an uncertainty framework.
Direct, inverse, cross and triangulated methods with an ordered chain, pivot currencies, per-step rounding permissions and an explicit conversion equation.

Basis code, defining authority reference, designating authority and market, session or scenario reference are carried; the technique itself, its inputs and its hierarchy remain with the valuation model.
Provisional, final, estimated and stale statuses, staleness tolerance with a named owner, exchangeability status and estimated-rate indicator, and a disputed state on failed recomputation.

Content digests over canonical serialisations bind the reproduction inputs to the stored result. Transport and at-rest protection are storage-projection concerns and are deliberately left to the projection and the adopting Dimension.

Separate authority declarations for amount correction, rate-source selection and rounding-policy change, distinguishing statutory mandate from entity policy, with a fallback path when a mandated source is unavailable.
Preparer, reviewer and approver distinctness is tested declaratively with an explicit relief-and-compensating-measure path, reflecting that smaller entities may be unable to segregate duties.

Digest, algorithm and computation time per evidence item, a manifest, defect and interested-party flags, publisher usage limitations, and audit references carried with an explicit non-assertion statement.

Sensitivity class, restriction basis, handling labels and projection constraints are declared as object attributes; whether a monetary value constitutes personal data is left to a referenced privacy model.

Strong validators with a required conditional predicate, a Dimension-fixed stale-validator outcome, and an idempotency key with published scope and expiry, fingerprint comparison, replay of the first outcome, a conflict outcome for in-flight duplicates and an unprocessable outcome for fingerprint mismatch.

A dedicated function renders every refusal as a machine-identifiable descriptor with a resolvable type, stable title, status, instance and extension members naming the target version and offending reference, plus a correlation reference for the audit component.

Exact decimal representation, retained rate significant figures, declared multiply-versus-divide operation, chain legs and quantisation order together make any derived value recomputable from its record.

Missing, stale, ambiguous and non-exchangeable rates, unsupported currency or code status, prohibited or invalid inverse, zero or non-positive rate, precision loss, out-of-tolerance reconciliation and lossy or suppressed export are all typed outcomes with severity and blocking indicators.

Suppression, secondary suppression, controlled and random rounding and interval publication are modelled as declared operations applied only under an external authorisation reference, with an information-loss statement and a reconcilability indicator.

Crypto-assets, central bank digital currency units, loyalty points and commodity units of account lack a governing identifier register equivalent to ISO 4217; the model can carry them only via an explicitly named alternative register, which is not specified here.

Cryptographic protection, transport security and key management belong to the storage and interface projections and to the adopting Dimension's security model; this model contributes only the content hash used for integrity of its own artifacts.

Deliberately excluded. A currency code does not encode country, jurisdiction or legal-tender territory, and the catalogue's country-name column is descriptive rather than a jurisdiction assertion; any geographic fact must come from a model that owns it.

known_omissions: The normative clause text of ISO 4217:2015 is behind a paywall; the structure rests on the Maintenance Agency's published machine-readable lists and public pages rather than on quoted clauses.

The clause text of IEEE 754-2019 is behind a paywall; only its published title, date and scope statement are relied on, with the publicly readable general decimal arithmetic model supplying the number model itself.

List Two, the fund codes registered with the agency, is published in a word-processing format and was not parsed in this pass, so registered fund-code specifics are thinner than those for the current and historic lists.
Digital-token and crypto-asset unit identity registers were not examined; non-ISO units are handled only through the generic mechanism of a declared alternative catalogue.
Jurisdiction-specific cash-rounding legislation was not surveyed; cash rounding is treated as locale and jurisdiction data owned elsewhere.
Unbounded and half-open monetary intervals are supported only through endpoint presence and inclusivity flags; no richer interval algebra was derived from sources.
No source was found that fixes a single maximum digit count for monetary amounts across domains, so digit bounds are left to the host or profile.

Indexed units of account and similar non-cash instruments are acknowledged only through the observation that the register assigns them codes and minor units; their revaluation semantics are not modelled here.
Historic non-decimal currency subdivisions are noted as a limit case, but no primary source governing their arithmetic was located within the evidence used.
Crypto-assets and other units outside the currency register are excluded; the sources used offer no maintenance-agency equivalent for their precision metadata.
The judgement of when a rounding difference stops being a residual and becomes an error is not modelled; the endorsed sources define materiality but set no monetary threshold.
The known-relation ledger for WM-XCT-032 is empty, so every composition link recorded here is a candidate requiring registry confirmation rather than an established contract.

No primary source was located that prescribes a universal allocation algorithm; the model requires the rule to be named and versioned but deliberately does not rank pro-rata against largest-remainder or sequential allocation.
Cash-rounding evidence covers only two jurisdictions; no attempt is made to enumerate every national increment, direction or mandate.

ISO 20022 CurrencyExchange element definitions (SourceCurrency, TargetCurrency, UnitCurrency, ExchangeRate, QuotationDate, ContractIdentification) and the currency-and-amount data types could not be retrieved from the ISO 20022 repository during this research; the alignment to payment-message currency exchange components is left as a gap and no clause is claimed.

The IOSCO Principles for Financial Benchmarks could not be retrieved (HTTP 403), so benchmark governance alignment rests on Regulation (EU) 2016/1011 and the FX Global Code alone; non-EU benchmark record-keeping expectations are therefore under-evidenced.
Digital assets, stablecoins and other units of account outside the ISO 4217 register are not addressed; a separate unit-of-account register and a distinct exchangeability model would be required.

Historic minor-unit changes, redenominations and non-decimal currencies are handled only by pinning the register version applicable at the valuation instant; no historic minor-unit table is modelled here.
Inflation-adjusted, index-linked and hyperinflationary restatement contexts are not modelled; they would need a restatement basis and an index reference beyond the current basis vocabulary.
Interval, range or probabilistic valuations with confidence bounds are not represented; the structure assumes a point value with declared accuracy.

Period-average and closing-rate expedients are represented only as rate types and series variations; the conditions under which an entity may use them belong to the accounting model and are not evidenced here.
Forward, swap and option-implied rates are referenced only as rate types; forward points, tenor and settlement conventions belong to the instrument and trade models.

The ISO 20022 repository could not be retrieved during this research; its ActiveCurrencyAndAmount constraints (total and fraction digits, currency attribute) are recorded as an unverified alignment and must be validated before any payments-message mapping is claimed.

ISO 4217:2015 and ISO 15489-1:2016 texts are behind paywalls and were not retrieved; currency code semantics were grounded in the maintenance agency's published lists and records-lifecycle structure in the NARA requirements instead.
US GAAP ASC 830 was not consulted, so the model records no evidence about its differences from IAS 21 on translation and remeasurement.
Hyperinflationary-economy restatement (IAS 29) and its interaction with valuation-date semantics are not represented.
Benchmark administration governance, such as the EU Benchmarks Regulation, was not verified; rate-source governance is treated only as a reference and a selection basis.
Non-ISO-4217 units of account - crypto-assets, loyalty points, vouchers, commodity-denominated units - are unresolved; the code-list pin assumes an ISO 4217 code space.
No cryptographic non-repudiation scheme (signature or trusted timestamping profile) is specified for approvals; only digest-based integrity is declared.

No local migration procedure for a currency redenomination or withdrawal that occurs while an effective interval is still open; the amendment record is referenced but the treatment of the straddling interval is undecided.
No rule for amounts denominated in a currency that lacks exchangeability, where an operational read must return the asserted value while accounting practice may require a different measurement.

Multi-currency composite assertions such as baskets and dual-currency instruments are not modelled; each currency is treated as a separate bound assertion and their mutual constraints are not expressed.
Cryptoassets and other units outside the ISO 4217 register have no register binding, so the currency-membership precondition cannot be evaluated for them.
No Dimension-wide default for sub-minor-unit scales such as unit pricing; the scale is declared per assertion with a reason, which permits inconsistent declarations across hosts.
The concurrency validator format is delegated to the host projection, so cross-host correction plans cannot always be compared or replayed.
Bulk operations — resolving or correcting many assertions atomically — are not specified; the contract addresses one assertion at a time.
Negative amounts, zero and signed-zero conventions are not constrained here; sign meaning is left to the host attribute path.
Hyperinflationary economy restatement and the interaction between restatement and translation are not modelled.
Interest, discounting, day-count conventions and present-value computation are excluded even though they produce monetary values.
Multi-currency netting, offsetting and settlement-risk computations are excluded.
Bid/ask/mid rate selection, spreads and dealer margin are not modelled as first-class parameters; they are treated as attributes of an externally supplied rate binding.
Historical redenomination factors for currencies replaced at a fixed ratio are referenced only through the register's successor code, not modelled as a conversion regime in their own right.

The precise ISO 20022 amount digit constraints could not be verified from a machine-extractable primary source at access time, so no specific total-digit or fraction-digit limit is asserted as normative here.
Tax and customs valuation rate mandates, which frequently differ from both accounting and reporting rates, are not enumerated.
conflicts: A widely used web vocabulary explicitly permits non-ISO currency identifiers such as cryptocurrency tickers and local exchange trading system names, while financial-messaging and clinical monetary datatypes bind currency to ISO 4217; this model resolves the conflict by requiring the catalogue to be declared rather than assumed.

Unicode CLDR states that its currency set deliberately diverges from ISO 4217, adding codes in widespread use and omitting some official ones, so CLDR membership is not evidence of ISO 4217 membership.

The ISO 4217 lists publish no applicable minor unit for precious metals, funds, testing and no-currency codes, while financial-message amount types constrain fraction digits by default; scale must therefore be declared explicitly and not inferred from the code.
CLDR cash digits and cash rounding differ from catalogue minor units, so no single decimal count is simultaneously authoritative for storage and for cash handling.
Historic withdrawal dates are published at month granularity or as month ranges, conflicting with the expectation that every recorded time is an RFC 3339 instant.

A public-authority reporting-rate list identifies currencies by country and currency description rather than by ISO code, showing that authoritative currency identity is catalogue-relative and that cross-register matching requires an explicit mapping.

Statutory euro-conversion rounding requires exact half-way results to be rounded up, whereas decimal arithmetic and much accounting practice default to half-even. The model therefore refuses to nominate a global default and requires the tie rule to be named per context.

Cash-rounding regimes quantize the total after tax to a five-cent increment while the same transaction settles to the cent electronically, so one underlying total legitimately yields two different payable amounts and a single canonical rounded amount does not exist.

Exchange profiles impose decimal limits that may be narrower or wider than the currency minor unit — for example two-decimal document amounts alongside unit prices with no decimal restriction, and an amount capacity of eighteen total and five fraction digits. Profile limits and currency minor units are independent constraints and can disagree.

Reporting accuracy is expressed with mutually exclusive decimal-place and significant-figure attributes, which does not map cleanly onto a single declared scale; the mapping is lossy in at least one direction and must be recorded as such.

The Canadian guidance fixes the increment and the cash-only scope but expresses direction as a fairness and transparency principle, while the Irish guidance fixes the endings explicitly. Direction is therefore not derivable from the increment alone and must be carried on the rule record.

The endorsed materiality definition consulted has since been consolidated into a later adoption regulation; the definition text is stable but the citation of record moves, so the model pins the instrument version rather than the concept.

Quotation direction conflicts between authoritative publishers: the ECB publishes all reference rates as EUR 1 = x foreign currency units, while the Federal Reserve H.10 publishes noon buying rates in New York for cable transfers payable in the listed currencies. Storing either as 'the rate' without explicit base, quote and direction produces silent inversion errors, which is why the published direction is canonical and inversion is a flagged derived field.

Revision-regime conflict: the Federal Reserve states that past H.10 releases are not revised and may not reflect subsequent revisions, whereas administrators under Regulation (EU) 2016/1011 operate methodology-change consultation and cessation procedures. A single provisional/final flag cannot represent both regimes, so the status code is qualified by the source identifier and its own regime.

Fitness-for-purpose conflict: the ECB states that its reference rates are published for information purposes only and that use for transaction purposes is strongly discouraged, yet adopting systems routinely use such rates for settlement conversion. The model records the source's stated restriction and surfaces it, but cannot prevent misuse, and this is a live governance risk rather than a solved one.

Precision conflict: XBRL guidance treats decimals='INF' as the correct expression of an exact monetary amount and warns that decimals='2' implies rounding, whereas many ledgers store amounts at the ISO 4217 minor unit and treat that storage as exact. The declared accuracy field must therefore distinguish exactness from rounding rather than record a decimal count alone.

Estimation conflict: IAS 21 as amended requires an estimated spot rate when a currency is not exchangeable but deliberately does not prescribe an estimation technique, so two standard-compliant asserters can record different rates for the same currency and instant. The model records the estimation approach reference and the estimated flag but cannot adjudicate between them.

Suspension conflict: the ECB suspended EUR/RUB reference rates from 1 March 2022 because it could not set a representative rate. A valuation requiring that pair after the suspension has no observable authoritative source, so a source-availability gap must be representable rather than silently filled by a stale or substituted rate.

The ECB publishes euro reference rates for information purposes only and strongly discourages transaction use, while the VAT Directive permits the latest published ECB rate for converting a taxable amount. A rate can therefore be legally mandated in one context and disclaimed by its publisher in another; the limitation note must travel with the value and must not be generalised into permission.

IAS 21 requires translation at the spot rate at the transaction date for the functional currency, while VAT Article 91 allows a Member State market rate, the ECB rate or customs-value rules. One economic event can carry two differently converted mandated amounts; the model records both with their profiles rather than reconciling them.

The ISO 4217 minor unit is a code-list attribute, not a rounding mandate. Statutory or contractual rounding may differ, so rounding is expressed as a pinned policy reference and never inferred from the minor unit.

A monetary fact identified only by concept, context and unit conflicts with master-data practice that expects a stable standalone identifier. This is resolved as weak host-dependent identity with conditional surrogates, which will break systems that assume a global monetary-value key.

Non-rewriteable preservation or audit-trail requirements for financial records conflict with in-place correction patterns common in operational systems; the model forces additive supersession, which increases storage and complicates naive last-write-wins synchronisation.

PCAOB expectations for segregated authorization, review and approval conflict with the practical staffing of smaller entities, so the model must permit an explicit relief declaration rather than assume full segregation.

Precision authority: the currency register fixes a minor unit per currency while payment and reporting payloads permit greater fraction digits, and one prominent payload type treats represented decimal precision as itself significant. Both are recorded; the declared scale governs locally and the minor unit is carried as a reference value.

Conditional-request semantics permit either a conflict or a precondition-failure outcome for a stale validator, and a widely used precedent returns either. The contract requires the adopting Dimension to fix one and publish it, since callers cannot branch reliably otherwise.

The idempotency key mechanism is an expired Internet-Draft, not a normative standard. Its conflict and unprocessable outcomes are adopted as a documented convention and explicitly not claimed as conformance.

Records-management practice differs on whether a superseded version is itself a record with its own retention trigger or merely a prior state of one record. The question is unresolved and produces an indeterminate readiness verdict with a blocker rather than a default.

Accounting standards require a foreign-currency transaction to be translated at the spot rate for the transaction date, while this contract forbids derivation in the read path. The two are reconciled by treating a translated figure as a separate referenced assertion, which some reporting pipelines will find surprising.

Provenance vocabularies distinguish revision of the same entity from derivation of a new one, while records systems often model both as versions of one record. The relation type is recorded explicitly so consumers can choose their interpretation.

EU law prohibits deriving an inverse rate for euro conversion, while the ECB publishes reference rates only with the euro as base currency; systems needing a non-euro base pair must either use a different source or accept a computation the euro regime forbids in its own scope. The model therefore makes inverse permissibility an explicit pinned parameter rather than a default.

IAS 21 requires the spot rate at the transaction date, whereas the U.S. Treasury regime mandates a single published rate for the reporting date and the ensuing three months, with amendments only when rates move by 10% or more. The same underlying transaction can legitimately carry different converted values under the two regimes.

XBRL 2.1 calculation checking effectively requires reported rounded figures to add up exactly, whereas Calculations 1.1 defines consistency by overlap of rounding intervals. A reconciliation verdict is therefore only meaningful once the tolerance basis is declared.

ISO 4217 minor units differ from the digit allowances of message profiles: a scheme profile may restrict a currency to two fractional digits while a message datatype allows more and the register defines a different minor unit for other currencies. Validation must be profile-pinned rather than register-only.

IAS 21 provides for estimating a rate when a currency is not exchangeable, which conflicts operationally with regimes that require an officially published rate; the model reports non-exchangeability as an outcome and refuses to substitute an estimate on its own authority.
regional_assumptions: The catalogue edition observed carries a published-edition marker of 2026-01-01 and already reflects a euro adoption effective that date; every adopter must pin its own edition rather than inherit this observation.
Minor-unit values published by the catalogue are catalogue facts about code structure, not statements about cash denominations circulating in any jurisdiction.
Legal-tender status, exchange controls and exchangeability are jurisdictional and time-varying, and are never inferred from a code or from the catalogue's country-name column.
Locale formatting, including decimal separator, grouping and symbol placement, varies by locale and forms no part of monetary identity or comparison.
Community, complementary and digital-asset units require an explicitly declared alternative catalogue; treating their tickers as ISO codes would be an error.
Cash-rounding evidence is drawn from euro-area and Canadian practice; other jurisdictions use different increments, directions and channel scopes, and some mandate rather than permit rounding.
The six-significant-figure conversion factor and triangulation rules are specific to the euro introduction and must not be generalised to arbitrary currency conversion.

Currency minor units reflect the maintenance agency's published list at a point in time; amendment activity around a euro adoption illustrates that a pin can go stale within a single reporting period.
Reporting accuracy attributes and e-invoicing decimal limits are drawn from one reporting language and one European e-invoicing profile; national filing formats may impose incompatible digit rules.
Materiality framing follows the endorsed international accounting definition; jurisdictions applying other frameworks may set thresholds on a different basis.

Publication semantics are drawn from euro-area practice (concertation around 14:10 CET, publication around 16:00 CET on working days except TARGET closing days) and United States practice (H.10 country data updated Mondays at 4:15 p.m.); other central banks publish on different sessions, conventions and calendars.

Benchmark governance references are EU-specific (Regulation (EU) 2016/1011); equivalent regimes elsewhere differ in scope, administrator obligations and supervisory reach, so the administrator reference must not be assumed to imply the EU obligation set.

An IFRS basis vocabulary is assumed for functional and presentation currency and for translation dates; jurisdictions applying national GAAP may use different role definitions and translation-date requirements.
Market calendars determine when no rate is published; a no-rate-available condition is calendar- and jurisdiction-dependent and cannot be inferred from a generic weekday rule.

The ISO 4217 register changes by dated amendment, including national euro adoptions with stated effective dates; the applicable register version is both region- and date-dependent and must be pinned per assertion.

Currency-pair convention evidence draws on BIS survey practice, in which both sides of a transaction are counted and the US dollar appears on one side of the large majority of trades; conventions in less liquid pairs may be locally determined.

EU rate-source rules are treated as one profile among several: Member States may mandate the most representative market rate, permit the latest published ECB rate subject to notification, or apply customs-value rules for defined categories.

US broker-dealer preservation periods and non-rewriteable or audit-trail requirements are treated as a jurisdiction-specific profile, not as a universal retention rule; other jurisdictions impose different periods.
The NARA electronic records lifecycle structure is used as a general lifecycle reference; it is a US federal programme requirement and is not binding outside that context.
IFRS is assumed only where a profile declares it; local GAAP profiles may assign different currency roles, rate bases and disclosure duties.
Currency code lists change by published amendment, so any assumption that a stored code is currently valid is jurisdiction- and time-dependent and must be resolved against the pinned edition.
No single global tax or accounting profile is assumed; precedence between competing profiles is an explicit decision recorded per value.

Hold and freeze semantics are drawn from a United States federal records authority: a freeze suspends scheduled disposition and is lifted only by a formal written request. Other jurisdictions use different instruments; the contract carries the reference and the effect, never the procedure.

Functional and presentation currency concepts follow IFRS. Jurisdictions applying other accounting frameworks may define the reporting currency, and therefore the meaning of the effective instant for reporting, differently.

Minor-unit expectations assume the ISO 4217 register. Jurisdictions with statutory cash-rounding rules, or with a legal tender whose practical smallest unit differs from the registered minor unit, must declare the rounding rule on the assertion.

Presentation conventions — decimal separator, digit grouping, symbol placement, negative-amount notation — are treated as locale projections and are excluded from the canonical form, which assumes a point decimal separator and no grouping.

The assumption that a records authority exists and can be referenced holds in regulated and public-sector settings; in lightly governed settings the retention-class reference will be absent and readiness will be indeterminate by design.

The six-significant-figure, no-inverse-rate and triangulation rules are specific to euro conversion under EU law and apply only to the euro and the national currency units it replaced; they are not a global default.

ECB reference rates are euro-based, published on TARGET working days only, explicitly discouraged for transaction purposes, and include suspended pairs; any deployment relying on them inherits those limits.

Treasury Reporting Rates of Exchange bind U.S. federal agencies and carry enumerated exceptions for collections, refunds and inter-currency conversions; they are not a general-purpose commercial rate source.

The 2026 transition of Bulgaria to the euro illustrates that register status and fixed conversion ratios are time-dependent; any validation must cite the register version in force at the valuation instant.
Statistical disclosure control terminology and thresholds follow European practice; other statistical authorities use different dominance rules and rounding bases.
adversarial_checks: Searched for any normative source that treats a currency symbol or localized name as an identifier; the opposite was found, with an explicit warning that the same symbol may denote several currencies, so symbols are modelled strictly as labels.

Tested whether a currency code alone determines the amount's scale; the register publishes no applicable minor unit for precious metals, registered funds, the testing code and the no-currency code, so a host-declared scale is required and a default of two fraction digits was rejected.

Tested whether binary floating point could be defended as the canonical representation; the exact decimal value space and the sign, coefficient and exponent number model rule it out, and no consulted source endorses it for monetary storage.

Tested whether zero could stand for an absent value; a published absent-reason vocabulary distinguishing unknown, masked, not-applicable, unsupported and error shows absence is a separate assertion, so the zero substitution was rejected.

Tested whether this mixin could own currency code allocation, withdrawal or reinstatement; the Maintenance Agency holds that authority, so succession and redenomination are carried as references and no local lifecycle, evaluation or enforcement machinery was modelled.

Tested whether comparison implies conversion capability; comparison was deliberately restricted to exact same-currency representations with an externally supplied compatibility assertion, and rate lookup, conversion and rate supersession were left with the rate publisher.

Tested whether the country column in the code list could support jurisdiction inference; it names entities associated with an entry rather than asserting legal-tender territory, so the spatial dimension was marked not applicable rather than quietly reused.

Tested whether an artifact could be justified for the amount itself; the amount has no identity or retention life independent of its host record, so only the externally published catalogue snapshot and amendment notice were declared as artifacts.

Two-decimal assumption: the structure was tested against zero-, three- and four-decimal currencies and against codes with no applicable minor unit. No data element or rule assumes a scale of two; minor units are read from a pinned list rather than inferred from a field width.

Single-rounding-rule assumption: the statutory half-up tie rule and the half-even accounting default were placed side by side. The model refuses to nominate a winner and makes an unnamed rule an explicit failure rather than a defaulted success.

Non-decimal increment: five-cent cash quantization was used to confirm that quantization is expressed as increment-or-exponent rather than as a digit count alone, and that channel scope is part of the rule rather than an afterthought.

Boundary creep into evaluation and audit: every bundle, layer, finding and function was re-read against the boundary notes and composition rationales. Quantization, allocation and comparison return values and signals to the caller and explicitly do not persist results, enforce policy or write audit entries; audit reconstructability is stated as a requirement placed on the adopting Dimension's facility, not as a capability owned here.

Boundary creep into rate sourcing: the comparison function was constrained to refuse incompatible values rather than convert them, and the conversion-precision question records declared factor and intermediate precision only. No element sources, selects, publishes or applies an exchange rate.

Registry duplication: the model was checked against the parent economic model's concern. Price, cost and valuation meaning were left with the parent and only representation, precision, quantization and comparison retained here.

Unsupported structure rejected: a proposed layer for rounding-error analytics and drift reporting was dropped because no primary source in scope governs it and it would have imported host analytics and monitoring into a mixin.

Identifier hygiene: every local identifier was checked for uniqueness across bundles, layers, findings, questions, data elements, artefacts and functions, and for the absence of any date-like component; version tokens and effective periods are held as attributes only.

Tested whether this model should own an exchange-rate time series, a rate determination methodology or a benchmark calculation. Rejected: ECB, Federal Reserve and Regulation (EU) 2016/1011 evidence all place determination, publication, methodology change and cessation with the source or administrator, so the model carries a reference, a binding and subject-specific parameters only.

Tested whether a rate value, currency pair or valuation date could serve as the identity of an amount. Rejected: the identity priority requires an authoritative master-system identifier, and a rate is a mutable context attribute whose correction must not change the identity of either amount.

Tested whether a valuation date alone is sufficient temporal context. Rejected: RFC 3339 requires seconds and an explicit offset for an instant, ECB rates are pinned to a concertation time and a separate publication time, and a single date cannot separate event, valuation, effective, publication and ingestion time.

Tested whether a single amount field with an attached rate is sufficient. Rejected: the IAS 21 functional-versus-presentation distinction and the requirement that the original remain retrievable force role-tagged sibling amounts with an explicit derivation link.

Tested whether holding reproducibility evidence makes this model the audit trail. Rejected: evidence packages carry references, parameters and a digest, while audit persistence, immutability enforcement, evidentiary weighting and retention execution remain with the referenced audit and retention models, and the correction function emits payloads rather than writing the audit record.

Searched for a counterexample in which a converted amount may legitimately replace the original. None found in the cited standards; even the lack-of-exchangeability case requires the estimated rate and its basis to be disclosed alongside the original rather than in place of it.

Tested whether any cited primary source sanctions folding a fee, spread or mark-up into a recorded exchange rate. No such support was found, so charge components remain separately referenced and an unexplained recorded-versus-source rate divergence is a validation failure.

Tested whether the rate-selection function could be presented as a policy engine. Rejected: the function applies caller-supplied criteria deterministically and records the outcome; policy authoring, approval, runtime evaluation and enforcement are left to the adopting Dimension's policy model.

Tested whether the model could set retention periods for its own records. Rejected: retention periods derive from the adopting Dimension's records policy and, where applicable, a reporting regime; the model carries a retention class, emits a disposition request and records the outcome reference only.

Searched for a normative requirement that every monetary value has an owner or a valuation authority. None was found, so role assignment is modelled as optional advisory metadata with explicit absence, rather than as a mandatory field that would fabricate accountability.

Tested whether the ISO 4217 minor unit can be presented as a rounding rule. The maintenance agency publishes it as a code-list attribute alongside alphabetic and numeric codes, so a rounding mandate was rejected and rounding was demoted to a pinned external policy reference.

Tested whether this model may hold audit conclusions or an audit trail. Audit evidence sufficiency and conclusions rest with the auditor and access logs rest with the authorization component, so only references and explicit non-assertion statements are carried; no audit-trail storage, evaluation or retention semantics are modelled locally.

Checked whether ECB reference rates could be treated as authoritative transaction rates. The publisher discourages transaction use, so rate-source declarations were required to carry a usage limitation instead of an implied permission.

Attempted to justify a local disposition workflow with destruction steps. The records lifecycle places disposal execution with the records programme, so only a readiness assessment, a hold declaration and a tombstone for this model's own records were retained.

Attempted to justify local access-decision logic so that restricted amounts could be masked by the model. Decision and enforcement are separated from attribute publication in both the access-control standard and the ABAC guide, so the model publishes attributes and declared projection constraints only and never records that masking occurred.

Tested whether a valuation date could serve as an identifier for repeated valuations of the same host amount. It cannot discriminate two valuations at the same instant from different sources, so identity was defined over host reference, role, currency and valuation context with a conditional surrogate.

Reviewed every bundle, layer, finding and function against each composition rationale for target-owned concepts. Rate determination, register amendment, measurement methodology, payment and posting, authorization evaluation, disposal execution and audit-trail semantics were all pushed to out-of-scope entries, boundary notes or reference links rather than modelled here.

Ownership probe: does any function persist, decide, enforce, destroy or produce an audit entry? Every function's effects list denies all five explicitly, and the delete rules name the external owner of each. The failure-description function emits a correlation reference rather than an audit record precisely so that referencing the audit component does not become owning it.

Lifecycle-creep probe: does any node define states for a currency, price, transaction, account, rate feed or instrument? No. States apply only to the assertion's version series, and currency withdrawal is read from the register as a status flag rather than modelled as a local transition.

Derivation probe: does any read or report compute a converted, rounded or re-scaled amount? No. The read finding forbids it, the policies restate it, and conversion is assigned to an external model by composition link. This is the check most likely to be violated by an implementation under pressure to be convenient.

Identity probe: does any identifier embed a date, amount or currency? No. Serial names use a monotonic per-series sequence, artifacts carry instants as content, and identifier reuse after tombstoning is barred.

Evidence probe: is any structural node asserted without primary support? Each bundle, layer, finding and function cites live primary sources. The idempotency convention is explicitly downgraded to a non-normative draft, and precision and jurisdictional questions are recorded as gaps rather than presented as settled.

Falsifiability probe: could an implementer disprove the read contract? Yes — the boundary convention, tie-break key, none-applicable outcome and forbidden derivations are stated concretely enough that two implementations returning different versions for the same as-of pair constitute a demonstrable defect.

Substitution probe: could a readiness report be mistaken for a disposition certificate? The delete rules and the artifact description both state it is never evidence that destruction occurred, and the tombstone excludes monetary content so that a surviving marker cannot be misread as a retained amount.

Checked every function against the ownership contract: none acquires a rate, moves money, posts to a ledger, persists a record, authorises disclosure, enforces a policy or writes an audit trail. The redaction function was specifically constrained to require an externally issued authorisation decision reference and to perform no evaluation of it.

Searched for counterexamples to a universal two-decimal assumption and found zero-decimal and three-decimal currencies in the register, a five-fraction-digit allowance in message datatypes and a two-decimal scheme restriction. The model therefore treats target scale as a pinned parameter with an explicit deviation authority rather than deriving it silently from the minor unit.

Tested whether the attractive shortcut of deriving an inverse rate could be presented as canonical; it could not, because EU law prohibits it within its scope while the only euro-base public source makes it operationally tempting. The conflict is recorded and the behaviour is made an explicit parameter with an emitted outcome when prohibited.

Tested whether a single tolerance constant could be presented as canonical for reconciliation; it could not, because interval-based and exact-sum consistency definitions coexist in the same standards family. Tolerance is therefore always declared with its basis, and a reconciliation without a declared basis is non-evaluable.

Checked whether the model was quietly claiming ownership of evidence and audit semantics through its validation output; it was, so the validation finding was reduced to inline transient results with the durable evidence record explicitly assigned to the external audit and records systems.

Checked whether redaction could be mistaken for deletion and closed the gap by stating that suppression never destroys the source value and that destruction requests are routed to the owning storage system.
